translations.idiomatic: The enemy retreated to the old camp at Sizhou; Yiyuan took it by assault, but the mobile corps commander Lu Degong was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 前逼新寨。

translations.literal: They pressed forward to the new stockade.
translations.idiomatic: They then advanced on the new stockade.

sentences.zh: 寨三面臨江，一面通陸，引海為濠，海艘泊寨下千計，築金海、固城為左右翼。

translations.literal: The stockade faced the river on three sides and had land access on one; seawater was drawn in as a moat; more than a thousand sea vessels moored below the stockade; Janghai and Gucheng were built as left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade faced the river on three sides with only one land approach; seawater formed its moat; more than a thousand ships lay below the walls; Janghai and Gucheng served as its flanking forts.

sentences.zh: 一元分馬步夾攻。

translations.literal: Yiyuan divided cavalry and infantry to attack from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyuan attacked with cavalry and infantry from both sides.

sentences.zh: 步兵遊擊彭信古用大棓擊寨，碎其數處。

translations.literal: The infantry mobile corps commander Peng Xingu used great battering beams against the stockade and smashed several places.
translations.idiomatic: The infantry commander Peng Xingu battered the stockade with heavy beams and breached several sections.

sentences.zh: 衆軍進逼賊濠，毀其柵。

translations.literal: The mass of troops pressed close to the bandit moat and destroyed their palisades.
translations.idiomatic: The army pressed to the moat and destroyed the palisades.

sentences.zh: 忽營中礮裂，煙燄漲天。

translations.literal: Suddenly a cannon in the camp burst; smoke and flames filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a cannon in the Ming camp exploded, filling the sky with smoke and flame.

sentences.zh: 賊乘勢衝擊，固城援賊亦至。

translations.literal: The bandits seized the momentum to charge; the Gucheng relief bandits also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy charged in the confusion, and reinforcements from Gucheng arrived as well.

sentences.zh: 騎兵諸將先奔，一元亦還晉州。

translations.literal: The cavalry generals fled first; Yiyuan also returned to Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The cavalry commanders fled first; Yiyuan withdrew to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔斬遊擊馬呈文、郝三聘，落信古等職，充為事官；

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered the mobile corps commanders Ma Chengwen and Hao Sanpin beheaded, Xingu and others reduced in rank and made officers on probation;
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, the mobile corps commanders Ma Chengwen and Hao Sanpin were executed, Peng Xingu and others were demoted to probationary officers,

sentences.zh: 一元亦奪宮保，貶秩三等。

translations.literal: Yiyuan also lost his Guardian title and was demoted three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: and Yiyuan was stripped of his Guardian title and demoted three ranks.

sentences.zh: 會關白死，倭遁走。

translations.literal: As it happened the kampaku died and the Japanese fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese regent died, the invaders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 石曼子為陳璘所殲，一元得還故秩，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Ishimanji was destroyed by Chen Lin; Yiyuan had his former rank restored and was given silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Ishimanji was destroyed by Chen Lin; Yiyuan's former rank was restored and he received silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died some years later.

sentences.zh: 一元歷鎮衝邊，並著勞績。

translations.literal: Yiyuan commanded in turn at strategic frontiers and distinguished himself with meritorious service everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyuan commanded several key frontier posts and distinguished himself in each.

sentences.zh: 與麻貴、張臣、杜桐、達雲為邊將選云。

translations.literal: He was ranked with Ma Gui, Zhang Chen, Du Tong, and Da Yun among the chosen frontier generals.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked with Ma Gui, Zhang Chen, Du Tong, and Da Yun among the finest frontier commanders of the age.

sentences.zh: 王保，榆林衞人。

translations.literal: Wang Bao was a man of Yulin Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao was a native of Yulin Guard.

sentences.zh: 驍勇絕倫，起行伍，積功為延綏參將。

translations.literal: His valor was unmatched; he rose from the ranks and through accumulated merit became assistant commander of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Fearless in battle, he rose from the ranks to assistant commander of Yan-sui through accumulated merit.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十六年遷延綏、定邊副總兵。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Wanli he was transferred to be deputy commander-in-chief of Yan-sui and Dingbian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Wanli he was appointed deputy commander-in-chief of Yan-sui and Dingbian.

sentences.zh: 十九年冬，擢署都督僉事，充昌平總兵官，尋改山西。

translations.literal: In the winter of the nineteenth year he was promoted to acting regional commander and appointed commander-in-chief of Changping, soon changed to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the nineteenth year he was promoted to acting regional commander and appointed commander-in-chief of Changping, then transferred to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 薊鎮總兵官張邦奇被劾，命保與易任。

translations.literal: The Jizhen commander-in-chief Zhang Bangqi was impeached, and Bao was ordered to exchange posts with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jizhen commander Zhang Bangqi was impeached, Bao was ordered to exchange posts with him.

sentences.zh: 自嘉靖庚戌後，薊鎮重於他鎮。

translations.literal: From the gengxu year of Jiajing onward, Jizhen was more important than the other garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Since the gengxu year of Jiajing, Jizhen had ranked above the other frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 穆宗有詔，獲大小部長者破格酬，他鎮不得比。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong had issued an edict that capturing great or minor tribal chiefs should be rewarded beyond the norm, which other garrisons could not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong had decreed extraordinary rewards for capturing tribal chiefs, a privilege denied other garrisons.

sentences.zh: 迨俺答款塞，宣、大、山西三鎮烽煙寂然。

translations.literal: When Altan submitted at the passes, the beacon fires of Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: After Altan submitted, the beacon fires of Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi fell silent.

sentences.zh: 陝西四鎮以火落赤敗盟，始復用兵，然寇弱易禦。

translations.literal: The four garrisons of Shaanxi, because Huoluo Chi broke the treaty, again took up arms, but the bandits were weak and easy to repel.
translations.idiomatic: The four Shaanxi garrisons resumed operations after Huoluo Chi broke the treaty, but the enemy was weak and easily managed.

sentences.zh: 獨泰寧、插漢諸部時時犯遼東。

translations.literal: Only the tribes of Taining and Chakhar repeatedly raided Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Taining and Chakhar tribes continued to raid Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 而薊門密邇王畿，與遼帥俱慎選。

translations.literal: Yet Jimen was close to the imperial domain, and together with the Liaodong commander its appointment was carefully chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Jimen lay close to the capital, and its commander, like the Liaodong commander, was chosen with special care.

sentences.zh: 以保有威望，用之。

translations.literal: Because Bao had prestige, he was employed.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was appointed on account of his prestige.

sentences.zh: 朶顏長昂當張臣鎮薊時納款。

translations.literal: Duoyan Chang Ang submitted when Zhang Chen commanded Jizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Duoyan Chang Ang had submitted while Zhang Chen commanded Jizhen.

sentences.zh: 居五六年，復連寇石門路、木馬峪、花埸谷，遂罷其市賞。

translations.literal: After five or six years he again raided in succession Shimen Road, Muma Valley, and Huachang Valley, and his market rewards were therefore suspended.
translations.idiomatic: After five or six years he raided Shimen Road, Muma Valley, and Huachang Valley in succession, and his market stipends were cut off.

sentences.zh: 後偕銀燈寇山海關。

translations.literal: Later he joined Yindeng in raiding Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Yindeng in raiding Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 已，又馳喜峰口要賞。

translations.literal: Before long he galloped to Xifengkou to demand rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode to Xifengkou to demand rewards.

sentences.zh: 邦奇佯許增市，誘殺其通事二十五人。

translations.literal: Bangqi pretended to agree to increase the market and lured and killed twenty-five of his interpreters.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi feigned agreement to expand trade and lured twenty-five of Chang Ang's interpreters to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 長昂益怒，犯大青山。

translations.literal: Chang Ang grew still angrier and raided the Great Green Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Ang grew furious and raided the Great Green Mountain.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遣其黨小郎兒等潛伏喜峰口，射殺偵卒。

translations.literal: Before long he sent his follower Xiaolan'er and others to lie in ambush at Xifengkou and shoot and kill scouting soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he sent his follower Xiaolan'er and others to ambush scouts at Xifengkou and kill them.

sentences.zh: 會保已至，遂禽之。

translations.literal: As it happened Bao had already arrived, and they were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had already arrived by then and captured them.

sentences.zh: 長昂每資小郎兒籌策，懼而謝罪，獻還被掠人畜，保乃釋還小郎兒。

translations.literal: Chang Ang always relied on Xiaolan'er for planning; he grew afraid and apologized, returned the people and livestock that had been seized, and Bao then released Xiaolan'er.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Ang had always relied on Xiaolan'er for counsel; frightened, he apologized, returned the captives and livestock, and Bao released Xiaolan'er.

sentences.zh: 長昂補五貢，邊吏始補二賞，互市如初。

translations.literal: Chang Ang made up five tribute payments, frontier officials then made up two rewards, and the border markets resumed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Ang made up five years of tribute payments, frontier officials restored two years of rewards, and trade resumed as before.

sentences.zh: 御史陳遇文援穆宗詔以請，進保署都督同知，副將張守愚以下皆進秩。

translations.literal: The censor Chen Yuwen cited Emperor Muzong's edict in his request; Bao was advanced to acting regional vice commander, and the deputy commander Zhang Shouyu and those below were all promoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Yuwen cited Emperor Muzong's edict in requesting rewards; Bao was promoted to acting regional vice commander, and Zhang Shouyu and his subordinates were all advanced in rank.

sentences.zh: 薊三協南營兵，戚繼光所募也，調攻朝鮮，撤還，道石門，鼓譟，挾增月餉。

translations.literal: The southern-camp troops of the three Jizhen sectors, recruited by Qi Jiguang, had been transferred to attack Korea; on withdrawal they passed Shimen, beat drums and made an uproar, and demanded increased monthly pay.
translations.idiomatic: The southern-camp troops of Jizhen's three sectors, raised by Qi Jiguang, had fought in Korea; on their return through Shimen they mutinied, beating drums and demanding higher pay.

sentences.zh: 保誘令赴演武場，擊之，殺數百人，以反聞。

translations.literal: Bao lured them to the drill ground, struck them, and killed several hundred, reporting it as a rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Bao lured them to the drill ground, attacked them, killed several hundred, and reported a rebellion.

sentences.zh: 給事中戴士衡、御史汪以時言南兵未嘗反，保縱意擊殺，請遣官按問。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Dai Shiheng and the censor Wang Yishi said the southern troops had never rebelled, that Bao had killed at will, and requested that officials be sent to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Dai Shiheng and censor Wang Yishi argued that the southern troops had never rebelled and that Bao had slaughtered them wantonly; they called for an official investigation.

sentences.zh: 巡關御史馬文卿庇保，言南兵大逆有十，尚書石星附會之，遂以定變功進保秩為真，廕子。

translations.literal: The pass-inspecting censor Ma Wenqing shielded Bao, alleging ten great treasons of the southern troops; Minister Shi Xing went along with it, and Bao was therefore advanced to regular rank for quelling the disturbance and his son was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Pass-inspecting censor Ma Wenqing shielded Bao, listing ten capital crimes against the southern troops; Minister Shi Xing concurred, and Bao was promoted to regular rank for suppressing the disturbance, with an enfeoffment for his son.

sentences.zh: 督撫孫鑛、李頤等亦進官受賜，時論尤之。

translations.literal: The governor-generals Sun Kuang, Li Yi, and others were also promoted and received gifts; public opinion especially blamed them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-generals Sun Kuang, Li Yi, and others were also promoted and rewarded; public opinion condemned them harshly.

sentences.zh: 二十三年冬，順義王撦力克弟趕兔率三軍犯白馬關及東西臺，為守備徐光啟，副將李芳春、戴延春所却。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-third year, Gantu, younger brother of the Shunyi Prince Bailingke, led three armies to raid Baimaguan and the eastern and western platforms; they were repelled by the garrison commander Xu Guangqi and the deputy commanders Li Fangchun and Dai Yanchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twenty-third year Gantu, younger brother of the Shunyi Prince Bailingke, led three columns against Baimaguan and the eastern and western platforms; garrison commander Xu Guangqi and deputy commanders Li Fangchun and Dai Yanchun repelled them.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，復偕部長倒布犯黑谷頂，敗而去。

translations.literal: The next autumn he again joined the tribal chief Daobu in raiding Heiguding, was defeated, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he joined the tribal chief Daobu in raiding Heiguding, was defeated, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 保度其再至，分營开連口及橫河兒。

translations.literal: Bao judged that they would come again and divided his camps between Kailiankou and Henghe'er.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting another raid, Bao divided his forces between Kailiankou and Henghe'er.

sentences.zh: [寇果馳橫河。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed galloped to Henghe.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders did gallop toward Henghe as expected.

sentences.zh: 官軍夜半疾抵石塘嶺，襲其營。

translations.literal: The government troops at midnight hastened to Shitang Ridge and raided their camp.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops reached Shitang Ridge at midnight and stormed the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 寇大驚潰，乘勢追出塞。

translations.literal: The bandits were greatly alarmed and fled in disorder; taking the momentum, the troops pursued them beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fled in panic and were pursued beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 其冬，復犯羅文峪，敗去。

translations.literal: That winter they again raided Luowen Valley, were defeated, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they raided Luowen Valley again, were defeated, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔代一元鎮遼東。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to replace Yiyuan in commanding Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him to replace Yiyuan as commander of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮再用師，敕保防海，卒於海州。

translations.literal: When troops were again sent to Korea, Bao was ordered by edict to defend the coast and died at Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were sent to Korea again, Bao was ordered to defend the coast and died at Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 贈左都督。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 子學書，宣府總兵官。

translations.literal: His son Xueshu was commander-in-chief of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xueshu became commander-in-chief of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 學詩、學禮並副總兵。

translations.literal: Xueshi and Xueli were both deputy commanders-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xueshi and Xueli both served as deputy commanders-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 學書既里居，守榆林城，拒李自成，不屈死。

translations.literal: After Xueshu had retired to his home village, he defended Yulin city, resisted Li Zicheng, refused to submit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After retiring home, Xueshu defended Yulin against Li Zicheng, refused to submit, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 杜桐，字來儀，崑山人，徙延安衞。

translations.literal: Du Tong, style Laiyi, was a native of Kunshan who moved to Yan'an Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tong, style Laiyi, was a native of Kunshan who settled in Yan'an Guard.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，由世廕累官清水營守備，以謀勇著。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, through hereditary privilege he rose to garrison commander of Qingshui Camp and was noted for his strategy and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli he rose through hereditary privilege to garrison commander of Qingshui Camp, renowned for strategy and courage.

sentences.zh: 遷延綏入衞遊擊將軍，改古北口參將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to mobile corps commander of the Yan-sui Inner Guard, then changed to assistant commander at Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as mobile corps commander of the Yan-sui Inner Guard, then as assistant commander at Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 用總督梁夢龍薦，擢延綏副總兵。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Governor-General Liang Menglong he was promoted to deputy commander-in-chief of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: On Governor-General Liang Menglong's recommendation he was promoted to deputy commander-in-chief of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 十四年就拜署都督僉事，充總兵官。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed acting regional commander and made commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed acting regional commander and commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時卜失兔以都督同知為套中主，威令不行，其下各雄長志常叵測。

translations.literal: At the time Bushitu as regional vice commander was lord of the Ordos, but his authority did not prevail; below him each chieftain was a strong leader whose intentions were often hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Bushitu held nominal authority over the Ordos as regional vice commander, but his power did not extend to the fractious chieftains below him.

sentences.zh: 朔漠素無痘症，自嘉靖庚戌深入石州，染此症，犯者輒死。

translations.literal: The northern deserts had never known smallpox; from the gengxu year of Jiajing, when they penetrated deep into Shizhou, they contracted this disease, and those who caught it died.
translations.idiomatic: Smallpox was unknown on the northern steppe until the gengxu year of Jiajing, when raiders who penetrated deep into Shizhou contracted it and died.

sentences.zh: 打兒漢者，卜失兔祖吉能部落也，數將命奉貢，累官指揮同知。

translations.literal: Da'erhan was of the tribe of Bushitu's ancestor Jining; he had repeatedly received orders to present tribute and had risen to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Da'erhan belonged to the tribe of Bushitu's ancestor Jining; he had repeatedly presented tribute and risen to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 一日互市還，與其儕禿退台吉等俱染痘死。

translations.literal: One day returning from the border market, he and his fellows Tutui Taiji and others all contracted smallpox and died.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from a border market one day, he and his fellows Tutui Taiji and others all died of smallpox.

sentences.zh: 禿退子阿計疑邊吏酖其父，思亂。

translations.literal: Tutui's son Aji suspected frontier officials had poisoned his father and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Tutui's son Aji suspected frontier officials had poisoned his father and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 及卜失兔西助火落赤共擾河西，諸部遂蠢動。

translations.literal: When Bushitu went west to aid Huoluo Chi in jointly harassing Hexi, the various tribes then stirred restlessly.
translations.idiomatic: When Bushitu went west to aid Huoluo Chi in raiding Hexi, the tribes grew restless.

sentences.zh: 十九年冬，打兒漢子土昧與他部明安互市訖，復臨邊要賞，聲犯內地。

translations.literal: In the winter of the nineteenth year, Tumai, son of Da'erhan, and Ming'an of another tribe, after finishing trade at the market, again pressed close to the frontier demanding rewards and threatened to raid the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the nineteenth year Tumai, son of Da'erhan, and Ming'an of another tribe, after trading at the market, pressed the frontier demanding rewards and threatened to raid inland.

sentences.zh: 桐與巡撫賈仁元計先出兵襲之。

translations.literal: Tong and the grand coordinator Jia Renyuan planned to send troops first to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Tong and grand coordinator Jia Renyuan planned a preemptive strike.

sentences.zh: 乃令參將張剛自神木，遊擊李紹祖自孤山，桐率輕騎自榆林，三道並出。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered the assistant commander Zhang Gang from Shenmu, the mobile corps commander Li Shaozu from Gushan, and Tong himself led light cavalry from Yulin; the three routes set out together.
translations.idiomatic: He sent assistant commander Zhang Gang from Shenmu, mobile corps commander Li Shaozu from Gushan, and led light cavalry from Yulin himself in a three-pronged attack.

sentences.zh: 遇寇力戰，大破之，斬首四百七十餘級，馘明安而還。

translations.literal: They met the bandits and fought fiercely, inflicted a great defeat, beheaded more than four hundred and seventy, took Ming'an's head, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They met the enemy in fierce battle, inflicted a crushing defeat, took more than four hundred and seventy heads including Ming'an's, and returned.

sentences.zh: 延綏自吉能納款，塞上息肩二十年，自此兵端復開。

translations.literal: In Yan-sui, since Jining's submission, the frontier had rested its shoulders for twenty years; from this the flames of war opened again.
translations.idiomatic: Yan-sui had enjoyed twenty years of peace since Jining's submission; now war resumed.

sentences.zh: 明安子擺言太日思報復，寇鈔無已時矣。

translations.literal: Ming'an's son Baiyantai daily plotted revenge, and raids and plunder knew no end.
translations.idiomatic: Ming'an's son Baiyantai sought revenge daily, and raids never ceased.

sentences.zh: 桐先被劾罷，以是役功，超授右都督，僉書後府。

translations.literal: Tong had earlier been impeached and dismissed; for merit in this campaign he was advanced beyond the norm to Right Regional Commander and made an assistant in the Rear Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Though previously impeached and dismissed, Tong was promoted to Right Regional Commander for this victory and appointed an assistant in the Rear Bureau.

sentences.zh: 二十一年以總兵官鎮保定。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he garrisoned Baoding as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was posted as commander-in-chief at Baoding.

sentences.zh: 二十四年徙延綏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 明年再徙鎮寧夏。

translations.literal: The following year he was again transferred to command Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to command Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 著力兔、宰僧入犯，逆戰水塘溝，俘斬百二十。

translations.literal: Zhuli Tu and Zaiseng invaded; he met them in battle at Shuitang Gully and captured or beheaded a hundred and twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuli Tu and Zaiseng invaded; he met them at Shuitang Gully and killed or captured a hundred and twenty.

sentences.zh: 寇益糾諸部連犯平虜、興武，桐督諸將馬孔英、鄧鳳、蕭如蕙等連破之，斬首二百餘級。

translations.literal: The bandits further gathered the tribes to raid in succession Pinglu and Xingwu; Tong supervised the generals Ma Kongying, Deng Feng, Xiao Ruhui, and others in successive defeats of them, beheading more than two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy gathered allies to raid Pinglu and Xingwu in succession; Tong directed Ma Kongying, Deng Feng, Xiao Ruhui, and others in repeated victories, taking more than two hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 而延綏將士亦數搗巢，諸部長懼，乞款，詞甚哀。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Yan-sui officers and soldiers also repeatedly struck their lairs; the tribal chiefs grew afraid and begged to submit, their words very pitiful.
translations.idiomatic: Yan-sui troops also raided their camps repeatedly; the chieftains grew afraid and sued for peace in pitiful terms.

sentences.zh: 三十年，二鎮撫臣孫維城、黃嘉善協謀撫之，乃復貢市。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the pacification officials of the two garrisons, Sun Weicheng and Huang Jiashan, cooperated in planning to pacify them, and tribute and markets were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year the pacification commissioners Sun Weicheng and Huang Jiashan negotiated peace, and tribute and trade were restored.

sentences.zh: 論功，文臣自內閣以下悉進官。

translations.literal: When merit was discussed, civil officials from the Grand Secretariat downward were all advanced in office.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were distributed, civil officials from the Grand Secretariat down were all promoted.

sentences.zh: 桐以先去職，但賚銀幣，許復用而已。

translations.literal: Tong, because he had left office earlier, received only silver and silks and permission to be employed again, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Tong had already left office and received only silver, silks, and permission to serve again.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒於家。

translations.literal: After a long while he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home some years later.

sentences.zh: 桐自偏裨至大帥，積首功一千八百，時服其勇。

translations.literal: Tong from junior officer to supreme commander accumulated a head count of eighteen hundred; his contemporaries admired his valor.
translations.idiomatic: From junior officer to supreme commander, Tong accumulated eighteen hundred heads; contemporaries admired his valor.

sentences.zh: 弟：松

translations.literal: Younger brother: Song
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Song

sentences.zh: 弟松，字來清。

translations.literal: His younger brother Song, style Laiqing.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Song, style Laiqing.

sentences.zh: 有膽智，勇健絕倫。

translations.literal: He had courage and wisdom, and his valor was unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and resourceful, his valor was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 由舍人從軍，累功為寧夏守備。

translations.literal: From cadet he joined the army and through accumulated merit became garrison commander of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a cadet and through merit rose to garrison commander of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十二年，卜失兔掠張春井，大入下馬關。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Wanli, Bushitu raided Zhangchun Well and made a major incursion into Xiamaguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Wanli Bushitu raided Zhangchun Well and made a major incursion through Xiamaguan.

sentences.zh: 松偕遊擊史見、李經以二千餘騎邀擊馬蓮井，小勝，誤入伏中，見戰死，松、經皆重傷，士卒死過半。

translations.literal: Song together with the mobile corps commanders Shi Jian and Li Jing with more than two thousand horsemen intercepted at Malian Well, won a small victory, mistakenly entered an ambush; Jian died in battle, Song and Jing were both seriously wounded, and more than half the soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Song and mobile corps commanders Shi Jian and Li Jing intercepted the enemy at Malian Well with two thousand horsemen, won a minor victory, then blundered into an ambush; Jian was killed, Song and Jing were badly wounded, and more than half their men died.

sentences.zh: 麻貴援軍至，松復裹創力戰，寇始敗走。

translations.literal: When Ma Gui's relief army arrived, Song again wrapped his wounds and fought fiercely; only then did the bandits flee in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Gui's relief force arrived, Song fought on despite his wounds and drove the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 時松已進遊擊將軍，論功遷延綏參將。

translations.literal: At the time Song had already been advanced to mobile corps commander; for merit he was transferred to assistant commander of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Song had already been promoted to mobile corps commander; for this action he was appointed assistant commander of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 貴大舉搗巢，松以右軍出清平塞，多所斬獲，進副總兵。

translations.literal: Gui launched a major strike at the enemy lairs; Song with the right wing went out from Qingping Pass, took many heads and captives, and was advanced to deputy commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Gui launched a major campaign against the enemy camps; Song led the right wing through Qingping Pass, took many heads and captives, and was promoted to deputy commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官改寧夏東路。

translations.literal: Soon with his present office he was changed to the eastern route of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned to the eastern route of Ningxia at the same rank.

sentences.zh: 松為將廉，尚氣不能容物。

translations.literal: Song as a general was upright, prized his honor, and could not tolerate others.
translations.idiomatic: Song was an upright commander, proud and intolerant.

sentences.zh: 常因小忿薙髮為僧，部議聽其歸。

translations.literal: He often shaved his head and became a monk over small resentments; the ministry deliberated and allowed him to return.
translations.idiomatic: He often shaved his head and became a monk over petty grievances; the ministry allowed him to return to lay life.

sentences.zh: 尋起孤山副總兵。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as deputy commander-in-chief of Gushan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as deputy commander-in-chief of Gushan.

sentences.zh: 三十三年擢署都督僉事，代李如樟鎮延綏。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was promoted to acting regional commander and replaced Li Ruzhang in commanding Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was promoted to acting regional commander and succeeded Li Ruzhang at Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 明年，套寇犯安邊、懷遠，松大破之，改鎮薊州。

translations.literal: The next year the Ordos bandits raided Anbian and Huaiyuan; Song inflicted a great defeat on them and was transferred to command Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Ordos raiders attacked Anbian and Huaiyuan; Song routed them and was transferred to command Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 三十六年夏，代李成梁鎮遼東。

translations.literal: In the summer of the thirty-sixth year he replaced Li Chengliang in commanding Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the thirty-sixth year he succeeded Li Chengliang as commander of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 十二月敗敵連山驛。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he defeated the enemy at Lianshan Post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he defeated the enemy at Lianshan Post.

sentences.zh: 賴暈歹者，朶顏長昂子也，狡黠為邊患。

translations.literal: Laiyundai was the son of Duoyan Chang Ang; cunning and sly, he was a frontier menace.
translations.idiomatic: Laiyundai, son of Duoyan Chang Ang, was cunning and a persistent frontier menace.

sentences.zh: 與從父蟒金潛入薊鎮河流口，大掠去。

translations.literal: With his father's younger brother Mangjin he slipped into the Jizhen river mouth and made a great raid before departing.
translations.idiomatic: With his uncle Mangjin he infiltrated the Jizhen river mouth and carried out a major raid.

sentences.zh: 復結黃台吉謀犯喜峰口。

translations.literal: He again joined Huang Taiji in plotting to raid Xifengkou.
translations.idiomatic: He then allied with Huang Taiji to attack Xifengkou.

sentences.zh: 松受總督王象乾指，潛搗黃台吉帳，以牽薊寇。

translations.literal: Song, on Governor-General Wang Xiangqian's instruction, secretly struck Huang Taiji's camp to draw off the Jizhen raiders.
translations.idiomatic: On Governor-General Wang Xiangqian's orders, Song secretly raided Huang Taiji's camp to draw off the Jizhen threat.

sentences.zh: 乃從寧遠中左所夜馳至哈流兔，掩殺拱兔部落百四十餘級。

translations.literal: He therefore from Ningyuan Middle Left Post rode by night to Haliutu and in a surprise attack killed more than a hundred and forty of Gongtu's tribe.
translations.idiomatic: He rode by night from Ningyuan to Haliutu and in a surprise attack killed more than a hundred and forty of Gongtu's followers.

sentences.zh: 以大捷聞，邀重賞，副使馬拯謂拱兔內屬，不當勦，彼且復讐，與松相訐。

translations.literal: When news of the great victory arrived, he demanded heavy rewards; the vice commissioner Ma Zheng said Gongtu was an inner subject and should not have been attacked, that he would seek revenge, and he quarreled with Song.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting a great victory, Song demanded heavy rewards; vice commissioner Ma Zheng argued that Gongtu was a subject tribe and should not have been attacked, warning of reprisals; he and Song quarreled bitterly.

sentences.zh: 松忿，邀賞愈急，詔予之。

translations.literal: Song grew angry and pressed for rewards ever more urgently; an edict granted them.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Song pressed ever harder for rewards; the court granted them.

sentences.zh: 拱兔果以無罪見勦怒，小歹青又數激之，乃以五千騎攻陷大勝堡，執守將耿尚仁支解之。

translations.literal: Gongtu indeed grew angry at being attacked without cause; Xiaodaqing repeatedly incited him; he therefore with five thousand horsemen attacked and took Dasheng Fort, seized the defending commander Geng Shangren, and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongtu, enraged at the unprovoked attack and goaded by Xiaodaqing, attacked Dasheng Fort with five thousand horsemen, captured the garrison commander Geng Shangren, and dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 深入小凌河，肆焚掠。

translations.literal: He penetrated deep into the Xiao Ling River region and burned and plundered at will.
translations.idiomatic: He penetrated deep into the Xiao Ling River region, burning and plundering at will.

sentences.zh: 遊擊于守志遇於山口，大敗，死千餘人，守志亦重創。

translations.literal: The mobile corps commander Yu Shouzhi met them at the mountain pass, suffered a great defeat, more than a thousand died, and Shouzhi was also seriously wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile corps commander Yu Shouzhi met them at a pass, was routed, lost more than a thousand men, and was badly wounded himself.

sentences.zh: 松駐大凌河，不敢救。

translations.literal: Song garrisoned the Da Ling River and did not dare to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Song remained at the Da Ling River and did not dare advance to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 遼人多咎松，朝議謂松前僅抵錦州邊十里，未嘗出塞，所殺乃保塞部落，悉縛殺之，非陣斬。

translations.literal: Many in Liaodong blamed Song; court opinion said that earlier Song had only reached ten li from the Jinzhou border, had never gone beyond the passes, and those he killed were tribes protecting the border—all bound and killed, not slain in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Many in Liaodong blamed Song; court opinion held that he had never truly crossed the border, that his victims were border-guard tribes bound and killed rather than slain in battle.

sentences.zh: 松愈忿，言撫按諸臣附會馬拯，害其奇功。

translations.literal: Song grew still angrier and said the pacification officials had gone along with Ma Zheng and harmed his extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: Song grew more furious, accusing the pacification officials of siding with Ma Zheng to deny him credit for a brilliant victory.

sentences.zh: 自提兵出塞，將搗巢以雪前恥，而所得止五級，士馬多陷大凌河。

translations.literal: He himself led troops beyond the passes, intending to strike the lairs to wash away his earlier shame, but obtained only five heads, and many troops and horses were lost at the Da Ling River.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops beyond the border to raid enemy camps and redeem himself, but took only five heads while many men and horses were lost at the Da Ling River.

sentences.zh: 松益慚憤，數欲自經，盡焚其鎧冑器仗，置一切疆事弗問。

translations.literal: Song grew ever more ashamed and angry, several times wished to hang himself, burned all his armor and weapons, and set aside all frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated and enraged, Song several times attempted suicide, burned his armor and weapons, and ignored all frontier duties.

sentences.zh: 兵部以聞，乃勒松歸里，而以王威代之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War reported this and ordered Song to return to his home district, replacing him with Wang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War reported this and ordered Song home, replacing him with Wang Wei.

sentences.zh: 松既廢，時多惜其勇，然惡其僨事，無推轂之者。

translations.literal: After Song was dismissed, many at the time regretted his valor, yet detested his ruining affairs, and no one recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: After Song's dismissal many regretted losing his valor, but his recklessness left no one willing to recommend him.

sentences.zh: 至四十三年，河套寇大入，令松以輕騎搗火落赤營。

translations.literal: By the forty-third year the Ordos bandits made a major incursion; Song was ordered to strike Huoluo Chi's camp with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year, when Ordos raiders invaded in force, Song was ordered to strike Huoluo Chi's camp with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 獲首功二百有奇，復敘用。

translations.literal: He obtained more than two hundred heads in merit and was again employed by seniority.
translations.idiomatic: He took more than two hundred heads and was restored to service.

sentences.zh: 逾二年，薊遼多事，特設總兵官鎮山海關，以松任之。

translations.literal: After more than two years, with many troubles in Ji-Liao, a special post of commander-in-chief to garrison Shanhaiguan was established, and Song was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, with troubles mounting in Ji-Liao, a special commander-in-chief post was created at Shanhaiguan and given to Song.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，張承廕戰歿，詔松馳援遼陽。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year Zhang Chengyin died in battle; an edict ordered Song to hurry to relieve Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year, after Zhang Chengyin was killed in action, Song was ordered to hurry to Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，楊鎬議四路出師。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year Yang Hao proposed a four-route expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The following February Yang Hao proposed a four-route expedition.

sentences.zh: 以撫順最衝，令松以六萬兵當之，故總兵趙夢麟、保定總兵王宣為佐。

translations.literal: Because Fushun was the most exposed, Song was ordered to meet it with sixty thousand troops; the former commander Zhao Menglin and the Baoding commander Wang Xuan served as his assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fushun was the most threatened route, Song was assigned sixty thousand men, assisted by the former commander Zhao Menglin and Baoding commander Wang Xuan.

sentences.zh: 期三月二日抵二道關，會李如柏等並進。

translations.literal: The plan was to reach Erdao Pass on the second day of the third month and join Li Rubai and the others in advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: The plan called for reaching Erdao Pass on the second day of the third month to join Li Rubai and the other columns.

sentences.zh: 松勇而無謀，剛愎使氣。

translations.literal: Song was brave but lacked strategy, stubborn and willful.
translations.idiomatic: Song was brave but rash, stubborn and willful.

sentences.zh: 二十九日夜，出撫順關，日馳百餘里，抵渾河。

translations.literal: On the night of the twenty-ninth he went out through Fushun Pass, galloped more than a hundred li in a day, and reached the Hun River.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the twenty-ninth he marched out through Fushun Pass, covering more than a hundred li in a day to reach the Hun River.

sentences.zh: 半渡，河流急，不能盡渡。

translations.literal: Halfway across, the river current was swift and they could not all cross.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway across, the current was too swift for the entire force to cross.

sentences.zh: 松醉趣之，將士多溺河中。

translations.literal: Song, drunk, urged them on; many officers and soldiers drowned in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Song urged them on; many officers and men drowned.

sentences.zh: 松遂以前鋒進，連克二小砦，松喜。

translations.literal: Song then advanced with the vanguard, took two small stockades in succession, and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Song advanced with the vanguard, captured two small stockades in succession, and grew confident.

sentences.zh: 三月朔乘勢趨撒爾湖谷口。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month he took the momentum and pressed toward Sa'erhu Valley Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month he pressed toward Sa'erhu Valley Mouth.

sentences.zh: 時大清方築城界凡山上，役夫萬五千，以精騎四百護之。

translations.literal: At the time the Great Qing was building a city on Jiefan Mountain; there were fifteen thousand laborers, guarded by four hundred picked horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing were then building a fort on Jiefan Mountain with fifteen thousand laborers guarded by four hundred picked horsemen.

sentences.zh: 聞松軍至，精騎則盡伏谷口以待。

translations.literal: Hearing that Song's army had arrived, the picked horsemen all lay in ambush at the valley mouth to await them.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Song's army was approaching, the Qing posted their best cavalry in ambush at the valley mouth.

sentences.zh: 松軍過將半，伏兵尾擊之，追至界凡渡口，與築城夫合據山旁吉林崖。

translations.literal: After more than half of Song's army had passed, the ambush force struck from the rear; they pursued to the Jiefan ford and, together with the fort builders, seized Jilin Cliff beside the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Once more than half of Song's column had passed, ambushers struck from the rear and pursued them to the Jiefan ford, joining the fort-builders in holding Jilin Cliff on the mountainside.

sentences.zh: 明日，松引大軍圍崖，別遣將營撒爾湖山上。

translations.literal: The next day Song led the main army to besiege the cliff and separately dispatched a general to encamp on Sa'erhu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Song brought up his main force to besiege the cliff and sent a detachment to camp on Sa'erhu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 松軍攻崖，方戰，大清益千人助之，已又續遣二旗兵趨界凡以為援，而遣六旗兵攻松別將於撒爾湖山。

translations.literal: Song's army was attacking the cliff and was in the midst of battle when the Great Qing added a thousand men to aid there; then it again sent two banners toward Jiefan as relief, while dispatching six banners to attack Song's detached commander on Sa'erhu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: As Song's troops assaulted the cliff, the Qing reinforced the defenders with a thousand men, then sent two banner contingents to relieve Jiefan while six banners attacked Song's detached force on Sa'erhu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 明日，六旗兵大戰，破撒爾湖山軍，死者相枕藉。

translations.literal: The next day the six-banner force fought a great battle, broke the Sa'erhu Mountain army, and the dead lay piled upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: The next day six banner regiments overran the Ming camp on Sa'erhu Mountain, leaving the dead piled on one another.

sentences.zh: 所遣助吉林崖者，自山馳下擊松軍，二旗兵亦直前夾擊，松兵大敗，松與夢麟、宣皆歿於陣。

translations.literal: Those sent to aid Jilin Cliff galloped down from the mountain to strike Song's army; the two-banner force also pressed straight forward in a pincer attack; Song's troops suffered a great defeat, and Song together with Menglin and Xuan all perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The relief force at Jilin Cliff charged down the slope into Song's ranks while two banner units struck from the front; Song's army collapsed, and Song, Zhao Menglin, and Wang Xuan were all killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 橫屍亘山野，流血成渠。

translations.literal: Corpses stretched across mountains and fields; flowing blood formed channels.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses covered the hills, and blood ran in streams.

sentences.zh: 大清兵逐北二十里，至勺琴山而還。

translations.literal: The Great Qing troops pursued north twenty li, reaching Shaoqin Mountain before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Qing troops pursued the fleeing Ming army twenty li to Shaoqin Mountain before turning back.

sentences.zh: 時車營五百尚阻渾河，而松已敗。

translations.literal: At the time five hundred chariot troops were still blocked at the Hun River, but Song had already been defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred chariot troops were still stranded at the Hun River crossing when Song's defeat became known.

sentences.zh: 頃之，馬林、劉綎兩軍亦敗，獨李如柏一軍遁還。

translations.literal: Before long the armies of Ma Lin and Liu Ting were also defeated; only Li Rubai's one army fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ma Lin's and Liu Ting's columns were routed as well; only Li Rubai's force escaped intact.

sentences.zh: 事聞，朝議多咎松輕進。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, court deliberations largely blamed Song for advancing rashly.
translations.idiomatic: When news reached the capital, court opinion largely blamed Song for his reckless advance.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，贈少保左都督，世廕千戶，立祠賜祭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Mentor and Left Regional Commander, with hereditary succession as a commander of a thousand households; a temple was erected and sacrifices granted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign Song was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Mentor and Left Regional Commander, with hereditary command of a thousand households, a memorial temple, and state sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宣亦贈官，立祠，世廕指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Xuan also received posthumous office, a temple was erected, and hereditary succession as battalion vice commander was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuan was likewise granted posthumous honors, a memorial temple, and hereditary battalion vice command.

sentences.zh: 宣，榆林人。

translations.literal: Xuan was a man of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuan was a native of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 夢麟，見父岢傳。

translations.literal: Menglin — see the biography of his father Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Menglin is treated in his father Ke's biography.

sentences.zh: 子：文煥 孫：弘域

translations.literal: Son: Wenhuan. Grandson: Hongyu.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Wenhuan. Grandson: Hongyu.

sentences.zh: 桐子文煥，字弢武。

translations.literal: Tong's son Wenhuan, style Taowu.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tong's son Wenhuan, style Taowu.

sentences.zh: 由廕敘，歷延綏遊擊將軍，累進參將、副總兵。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he rose through the posts of Yan-sui mobile corps commander and was progressively promoted to assistant commander and deputy commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Entering service through hereditary privilege, he rose to mobile corps commander of Yan-sui and was progressively promoted to assistant commander and deputy commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四十三年擢署都督僉事、寧夏總兵官。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was promoted to acting regional commander and commander-in-chief of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was appointed acting regional commander and commander-in-chief of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 延綏被寇，文煥赴救，大破之。

translations.literal: Yan-sui was raided; Wenhuan hurried to the rescue and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan-sui came under attack, Wenhuan rushed to its relief and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 明年遂代官秉忠鎮延綏。

translations.literal: The following year he then replaced Guan Bingzhong in commanding Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he succeeded Guan Bingzhong as commander of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 屢敗寇安邊、保寧，長樂，斬首三百有奇。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated bandits at Anbian, Baoning, and Changle, beheading more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly defeated raiders at Anbian, Baoning, and Changle, taking more than three hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 西路火落赤、卜言太懼，相率降。

translations.literal: Huoluo Chi and Buyantai of the western route grew afraid and submitted together in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Huoluo Chi and Buyantai on the western front grew afraid and surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 沙計數盜邊，為文煥所敗，遂納款。

translations.literal: Shaji repeatedly raided the border and was defeated by Wenhuan; he then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shaji, who had repeatedly raided the frontier, was defeated by Wenhuan and submitted.

sentences.zh: 既而復與吉能、明愛合，駐高家、柏林邊，要封王、補賞十事。

translations.literal: Before long he again joined with Jining and Ming'ai, encamped at the Gaojia and Bolin frontier, and demanded enfeoffment as king and ten items of supplementary rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Jining and Ming'ai again, encamped along the Gaojia and Bolin frontier, and demanded princely rank plus ten other concessions.

sentences.zh: 文煥襲其營，斬首百五十。

translations.literal: Wenhuan raided their camp and beheaded a hundred and fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhuan raided their camp and took a hundred and fifty heads.

sentences.zh: 火落赤諸部落攢刀立誓，獻罰九九。

translations.literal: The tribes under Huoluo Chi piled up swords and swore oaths, presenting punitive fines of nine-times-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Huoluo Chi's tribes stacked swords to swear peace and offered fines of nine-nine.

sentences.zh: 九九者，部落中罰駝馬牛羊數也。

translations.literal: Nine-nine was the number of camels, horses, cattle, and sheep as fines within the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: "Nine-nine" denoted the customary tribal fine in camels, horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 已，沙計又伏兵沙溝，誘殺都指揮王國安，糾猛克什力犯雙山堡，復犯波羅。

translations.literal: Later Shaji again hid troops in Shagou, lured and killed regional commander Wang Guo'an, rallied Mengkeshili to attack Shuangshan Fort, and again raided Boluo.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shaji ambushed troops in Shagou, lured and killed regional commander Wang Guo'an, rallied Mengkeshili against Shuangshan Fort, and raided Boluo again.

sentences.zh: 文煥擊破之，追奔二十餘里。

translations.literal: Wenhuan struck and defeated them, pursuing the fleeing enemy more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhuan routed them and pursued the fugitives more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 當是時，套寇號十萬。

translations.literal: At this time the Ordos bandits were said to number a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the Ordos raiders were said to number a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 然其衆分四十二枝，多者二三千，少不及千騎，屢不得志。

translations.literal: Yet their forces were divided into forty-two branches; the larger had two or three thousand, the smaller fewer than a thousand horsemen, and they repeatedly failed to achieve their aims.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were split into forty-two bands of no more than two or three thousand horsemen each—and many fewer than a thousand—and repeatedly failed to gain their ends.

sentences.zh: 沙計乃與吉能、明愛、猛克什力相繼納款，延綏遂少事。

translations.literal: Shaji then submitted together with Jining, Ming'ai, and Mengkeshili in succession, and Yan-sui then had few troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Shaji, Jining, Ming'ai, and Mengkeshili submitted in turn, and Yan-sui enjoyed a respite from trouble.

sentences.zh: 文煥尋以疾歸。

translations.literal: Before long Wenhuan returned home due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhuan soon retired home due to illness.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年再鎮延綏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he again commanded Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi he was again appointed commander of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 詔文煥援遼，文煥乃遣兵出河套，搗巢以致寇。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wenhuan to relieve Liaodong; Wenhuan therefore sent troops out into the Ordos to strike their lairs in order to draw the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to reinforce Liaodong, Wenhuan sent troops into the Ordos to raid enemy camps and draw off the raiders.

sentences.zh: 諸部大恨，深入固原、慶陽，圍延安，揚言必縛文煥，掠十餘日始去。

translations.literal: The tribes greatly resented this; they penetrated deep into Guyuan and Qingyang, besieged Yan'an, declared they would certainly bind Wenhuan, plundered for more than ten days, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were furious; they penetrated deep into Guyuan and Qingyang, besieged Yan'an, vowed to capture Wenhuan, and plundered for more than ten days before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 命解職候勘。

translations.literal: He was ordered removed from office pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 奢崇明圍成都，總督張我續請令文煥赴救。

translations.literal: She Chongming besieged Chengdu; Governor-General Zhang Woxu requested that Wenhuan be sent to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When She Chongming besieged Chengdu, Governor-General Zhang Woxu requested that Wenhuan be sent to the relief.

sentences.zh: 至則圍已解，偕諸軍復重慶。

translations.literal: When he arrived the siege had already been lifted; he joined the armies in recovering Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived the siege had ended; he joined the army in retaking Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 崇明遁永寧，文煥頓不進。

translations.literal: Chongming fled to Yongning; Wenhuan halted and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Chongming fled to Yongning, but Wenhuan halted and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 尋擢總理，盡統川、貴、湖廣軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to general commander and fully commanded the armies of Sichuan, Guizhou, and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to supreme commander with authority over all troops in Sichuan, Guizhou, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 度不能制賊，謝病去。

translations.literal: Judging that he could not subdue the bandits, he pleaded illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Concluding he could not suppress the rebels, he pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 坐延綏失事罪，戍邊。

translations.literal: He was punished for the Yan-sui disaster and sent to garrison duty on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for the Yan-sui debacle and banished to frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 七年起鎮寧夏。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was again appointed to command Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was reappointed commander of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 寧、錦告警，詔文煥馳援，俄令分鎮寧遠。

translations.literal: When Ningxia and Jinzhou sent alarms, an edict ordered Wenhuan to hurry to the relief; soon he was ordered to divide command and garrison Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningxia and Jinzhou came under attack, Wenhuan was ordered to hurry to their relief and soon afterward to assume separate command at Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 進右都督，調守關門。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Regional Commander and transferred to guard the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Regional Commander and transferred to defend the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 尋引疾去。

translations.literal: Soon he pleaded illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 子弘域，天啟初歷延綏副總兵。

translations.literal: His son Hongyu, at the beginning of Tianqi, served as deputy commander-in-chief of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongyu served as deputy commander-in-chief of Yan-sui early in the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，文煥援遼，即擢總兵官，代鎮寧夏。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year, as Wenhuan went to relieve Liaodong, Hongyu was immediately promoted to commander-in-chief and replaced him in commanding Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventh year, when Wenhuan marched to reinforce Liaodong, Hongyu was promoted to commander-in-chief and succeeded him at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 積資至右都督。

translations.literal: Through accumulated seniority he rose to Right Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Through seniority he rose to Right Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，提督池河、浦口二營練兵，遏賊南渡，頗有功。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen era he supervised the Chihe and Pukou camps in training troops, blocking the bandits from crossing south, and achieved considerable merit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he trained troops at the Chihe and Pukou camps, blocking rebel crossings south of the Yangtze with considerable success.

sentences.zh: 十三年移鎮浙江。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to command Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to command Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 尋謝病去。

translations.literal: Soon he pleaded illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 國變後，文煥父子歸原籍崑山，卒。

translations.literal: After the dynastic change, Wenhuan and his son returned to their ancestral home in Kunshan and died.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty, Wenhuan and Hongyu returned to their ancestral home in Kunshan, where they died.

sentences.zh: 蕭如薰

translations.literal: Xiao Ruxun
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ruxun

sentences.zh: 蕭如薰，字季馨，延安衞人。

translations.literal: Xiao Ruxun, style Jixin, was a man of Yan'an Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ruxun, style Jixin, was a native of Yan'an Guard.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，由世廕百戶歷官寧夏參將，守平虜城。

translations.literal: In the Wanli era, through hereditary privilege as a company commander he rose to Ningxia assistant commander and defended Pinglu city.
translations.idiomatic: During Wanli he entered service as a hereditary company commander, rose to assistant commander of Ningxia, and defended Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，哱拜、劉東暘據寧夏鎮城反，遣其黨四出略地。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year, Pubai and Liu Dongyang seized Ningxia garrison city in rebellion and sent their followers out in all directions to seize territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twentieth year Pubai and Liu Dongyang seized the Ningxia garrison and rebelled, sending their followers to seize territory in all directions.

sentences.zh: 拜子承恩徇玉泉營，遊擊傅桓拒守，為其下所執。

translations.literal: Pai's son Chengen marched on Yuquan Camp; the mobile corps commander Fu Huan defended and was seized by his own subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Pubai's son Chengen marched on Yuquan Camp; mobile corps commander Fu Huan tried to hold out but was seized by his own men.

sentences.zh: 賊已徇中衞及廣武，參將熊國臣等棄城奔，列城皆風靡。

translations.literal: The bandits had already marched on Zhongwei and Guangwu; assistant commanders Xiong Guochen and others abandoned their cities and fled, and city after city collapsed like before the wind.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already taken Zhongwei and Guangwu; assistant commanders including Xiong Guochen fled their posts, and city after city fell without resistance.

sentences.zh: 賊黨土文秀徇平虜，獨如薰堅守不下。

translations.literal: The rebel partisan Tu Wenxiu marched on Pinglu, but Ruxun alone held firm and the city did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leader Tu Wenxiu attacked Pinglu, but Ruxun alone held the city.

sentences.zh: 如薰妻楊氏，故尚書兆女也，賢而有智，贊夫死守，日具牛酒犒士。

translations.literal: Ruxun's wife Lady Yang, daughter of the former minister Zhao, was virtuous and intelligent; she assisted her husband in holding to the death and daily prepared oxen and wine to reward the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun's wife Lady Yang, daughter of a former minister of the Zhao surname, was intelligent and capable; she helped her husband hold the city and daily provided beef and wine to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 拜養子雲最驍勇，引河套著力兔急攻。

translations.literal: Pai's adopted son Yun was the most fierce and brave; he brought Zhuli Tu of the Ordos for a swift attack.
translations.idiomatic: Pubai's adopted son Yun, the fiercest of the rebels, brought Ordos chieftain Zhuli Tu for a furious assault.

sentences.zh: 如薰伏兵南關，佯敗，誘賊入，射雲死，餘衆敗去。

translations.literal: Ruxun hid troops at the south gate, feigned defeat, lured the bandits in, shot Yun dead, and the remaining force fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun posted ambush troops at the south gate, feigned retreat, lured the rebels in, and killed Yun with an arrow; the rest fled.

sentences.zh: 又襲著力兔營，獲人畜甚多。

translations.literal: He again raided Zhuli Tu's camp and captured a great many people and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: He then raided Zhuli Tu's camp and took many captives and livestock.

sentences.zh: 著力兔憤，復來攻，為麻貴所却，城獲全。

translations.literal: Zhuli Tu grew angry and attacked again; he was repelled by Ma Gui, and the city was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Zhuli Tu attacked again but was driven off by Ma Gui, and the city was saved.

sentences.zh: 初，帝聞如薰孤城抗賊，大喜，厚賚銀幣，擢官副總兵。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor heard that Ruxun in an isolated city resisted the bandits, he was greatly pleased, richly rewarded silver and silks, and promoted him to deputy commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned that Ruxun was holding an isolated city against the rebels, he was delighted, richly rewarded him with silver and silks, and promoted him to deputy commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 六月遂以都督僉事為寧夏總兵官，盡統延綏、甘肅、固原諸援軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was then made Ningxia commander-in-chief as regional commander and fully commanded the relief armies of Yan-sui, Gansu, and Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was appointed Ningxia commander-in-chief as regional commander, commanding all relief forces from Yan-sui, Gansu, and Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 其秋竟與李如松等共平賊，再進署都督同知，廕錦衣世指揮僉事；

translations.literal: That autumn he finally together with Li Rusong and others jointly pacified the bandits, was further advanced to acting regional vice commander, and granted hereditary succession as battalion vice commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard;
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he joined Li Rusong and others in suppressing the rebellion, was promoted to acting regional vice commander, and granted hereditary battalion vice command in the Embroidered Uniform Guard;

sentences.zh: 妻楊氏亦被旌。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Yang was also commended.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang was also honored for her service.

sentences.zh: 二十二年八月，卜失兔西犯定邊，闌入固原塞，副將姜直不能禦，遂由沙梁隤牆入，直抵下馬關，縱橫內地幾一月。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-second year Bushitu raided west toward Dingbian, broke into Guyuan Pass, deputy commander Jiang Zhi could not resist; he then entered through Shaliang by collapsing the wall, reached straight to Xiamaguan, and ranged across the interior for nearly a month.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-second year Bushitu struck west at Dingbian, broke through Guyuan Pass when Deputy Commander Jiang Zhi failed to stop him, breached the wall at Shaliang, raided as far as Xiamaguan, and ravaged the interior for nearly a month.

sentences.zh: 如薰免官，直下吏。

translations.literal: Ruxun was removed from office and immediately handed over to judicial officers.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun was dismissed and turned over to the courts.

sentences.zh: 尋復以總兵官鎮守固原。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed commander-in-chief to garrison Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed commander-in-chief at Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 套寇入犯，擊却之。

translations.literal: Ordos bandits invaded; he struck and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: When Ordos raiders invaded, he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 青海寇糾番族犯洮、岷，如黨及臨洮總兵孫仁禦之，禽斬三百四十有奇，撫叛番五千人，獲駝馬甲仗無算。

translations.literal: Qinghai bandits rallied fan tribes to raid Tao and Min; Ruxun together with Lin-tao commander-in-chief Sun Ren defended against them, captured and beheaded more than three hundred and forty, pacified five thousand rebellious fan tribes, and obtained countless camels, horses, armor, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinghai raiders rallied Tibetan tribes against Tao and Min, Ruxun and Lin-tao commander Sun Ren repulsed them, killing or capturing more than three hundred and forty, pacifying five thousand rebels, and seizing countless camels, horses, armor, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 再鎮寧夏。

translations.literal: He again commanded Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed commander of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 銀定、歹成數入犯，輒挫衂去。

translations.literal: Yinding and Daicheng repeatedly invaded and were repeatedly frustrated and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Yinding and Daicheng raided repeatedly but were repulsed each time.

sentences.zh: 徙鎮薊州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，罷歸。

translations.literal: After a long while he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 再起故官，鎮延綏。

translations.literal: He was again raised to his former office and commanded Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to his former rank and appointed commander of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，廷議京軍不足用，召邊將分營訓練。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, the court debated that capital troops were insufficient; frontier generals were summoned to train troops in separate camps.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi the court decided that capital garrisons were inadequate and summoned frontier generals to train troops in separate camps.

sentences.zh: 如薰典神機營。

translations.literal: Ruxun supervised the Shenji Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun was put in charge of the Firearms Brigade.

sentences.zh: 陛見，帝賜食加奬勞焉。

translations.literal: On audience at court, the emperor granted him food and added commendation and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: On presenting himself at court, the emperor granted him a feast and special commendation.

sentences.zh: 明年出鎮徐州。

translations.literal: The following year he went out to command Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was posted to command Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄召還京，復以總兵官鎮守保定。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to the capital and again served as commander-in-chief garrisoning Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to Beijing and reappointed commander-in-chief at Baoding.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，魏忠賢黨劾其與李三才聯姻，遂奪職。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year, eunuch Wei Zhongxian's faction impeached him for marrying into Li Sancai's family, and his office was then stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year, partisans of Wei Zhongxian impeached him for marrying into Li Sancai's family, and he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初卒，賜恤如制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he died; posthumous condolences were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Chongzhen reign and was granted posthumous honors according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 如薰為將持重。

translations.literal: Ruxun as a general was steady and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander Ruxun was steady and deliberate.

sentences.zh: 更歷七鎮，所在見稱。

translations.literal: He successively served seven garrisons and was praised wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: He served seven garrisons in succession and won praise at each posting.

sentences.zh: 自隆慶後，款市既成，烽燧少警，輦下視鎮帥為外府。

translations.literal: Since Longqing, once tribute markets were established, beacon fires were rarely alarmed, and the capital regarded garrison commanders as officials of an outer prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Since Longqing, with border markets established and alarms few, the capital treated frontier commanders as provincial officials of little account.

sentences.zh: 山人雜流，乞朝士尺牘往者，無不饜所欲。

translations.literal: Mountain recluses and miscellaneous wanderers who begged letters from court officials to go to them invariably had their desires fully satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Recluses and hangers-on who carried letters of introduction from court officials invariably got whatever they asked for.

sentences.zh: 薊鎮戚繼光有能詩名，尤好延文士，傾貲結納，取足軍府。

translations.literal: Jizhen's Qi Jiguang had a reputation for poetic talent, especially loved to host literary gentlemen, poured out his wealth in cultivating connections, and drew fully from the military commandery's resources.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhen commander Qi Jiguang was famed for his poetry and lavish hospitality to scholars, spending freely and drawing heavily on military funds.

sentences.zh: 如薰亦能詩，士趨之若騖，賓座常滿。

translations.literal: Ruxun also could compose poetry; gentlemen rushed to him as if racing, and his guest seats were constantly full.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun also wrote poetry, and scholars flocked to him; his table was always full of guests.

sentences.zh: 妻楊氏、繼妻南氏皆貴家女，至脫簪珥供客猶不給。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Yang and his successor wife Lady Nan were both daughters of noble families; they even removed hairpins and earrings to supply guests yet still could not meet the need.
translations.idiomatic: His wives Lady Yang and Lady Nan, both from prominent families, stripped off their jewelry to entertain guests and still could not keep up with the expense.

sentences.zh: 軍中患苦之，如薰莫能却也。

translations.literal: The army suffered bitterly from this; Ruxun could not refuse them.
translations.idiomatic: The troops suffered under the expense, yet Ruxun could not turn guests away.

sentences.zh: 一時風會所尚，諸邊物力為耗，識者歎焉。

translations.literal: This was what the fashion of the time admired; resources on the various frontiers were depleted, and those who understood sighed over it.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the fashion of the age, and frontier resources were drained dry—observers could only sigh.

sentences.zh: 如薰祖漢，涼州副總兵、都督僉事。

translations.literal: Ruxun's grandfather Han was deputy commander-in-chief of Liangzhou and regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ruxun's grandfather Han was deputy commander-in-chief of Liangzhou and regional commander.

sentences.zh: 父文奎，京營副將、都督同知。

translations.literal: His father Wen Kui was deputy general of the Capital Garrison and regional vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wen Kui was deputy general of the Capital Garrison and regional vice commander.

sentences.zh: 兄如蘭，陝西副總兵、都督僉事，前府僉書；

translations.literal: His elder brother Rulan was deputy commander-in-chief of Shaanxi and regional commander, assistant in the Front Bureau;
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Rulan was deputy commander-in-chief of Shaanxi, regional commander, and an assistant in the Front Bureau;

sentences.zh: 如蕙，寧夏總兵官、都督同知；

translations.literal: Ruhui was commander-in-chief of Ningxia and vice regional commander;
translations.idiomatic: Ruhui served as commander-in-chief of Ningxia and vice regional commander;

sentences.zh: 如芷，提督南京教場、都督僉事。

translations.literal: Ruzhi was superintendent of the Nanjing training ground and assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhi was superintendent of the Nanjing training ground and assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 達雲，涼州衞人。

translations.literal: Da Yun was a native of Liangzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Da Yun was a native of Liangzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 勇悍饒智略。

translations.literal: Bold and fierce, rich in strategic skill.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and fierce, and possessed no small share of cunning.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，嗣世職指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he inherited the hereditary post of assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he inherited the hereditary office of assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 擢守備，進肅州遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to garrison commandant and advanced to mobile corps commander of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to garrison commandant, then to mobile corps commander at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 炒胡兒入犯，偕參將楊濬擊敗之，遷西寧參將。

translations.literal: When Chao Hu'er invaded, together with assistant commander Yang Jun he defeated them and was transferred to assistant commander at Xining.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao Hu'er raided the border, he joined assistant commander Yang Jun in defeating the invaders and was transferred to Xining as assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 永邵卜者，順義王俺答從子也，部衆強盛。

translations.literal: Yong Shaobu was a nephew of Altan, Prince of Shunyi; his followers were strong and numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Shaobu was a nephew of Altan, Prince of Shunyi, and commanded a strong and numerous following.

sentences.zh: 先嘗授都督同知，再進龍虎將軍。

translations.literal: He had first been granted the title of vice regional commander and later promoted to Tiger-and-Dragon General.
translations.idiomatic: He had previously received the rank of vice regional commander and was later promoted to Tiger-and-Dragon General.

sentences.zh: 自以貢市在宣府，守臣遇己厚，不可逞，乃隨俺答西迎活佛，留據青海，與瓦剌他卜囊歲為西寧患。

translations.literal: Deeming that the tribute market was at Xuanfu and that frontier officials treated him generously so that he could not show his strength, he followed Altan west to welcome the Living Buddha, remained occupying Qinghai, and with the Oirat Tabunang became a yearly scourge to Xining.
translations.idiomatic: Because the tribute market lay at Xuanfu and frontier officials treated him well, he could not raid there as he wished; instead he followed Altan west to welcome the Living Buddha, seized Qinghai, and together with the Oirat Tabunang troubled Xining year after year.

sentences.zh: 嘗誘殺副將李魁。

translations.literal: He once lured and killed deputy commander Li Kui.
translations.idiomatic: He had once lured deputy commander Li Kui to his death.

sentences.zh: 邊臣不能報，益有輕中國心。

translations.literal: Frontier officials could not avenge it, and he increasingly held a heart of looking down on China.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials could not retaliate, and he grew ever bolder in his contempt for the Ming.

sentences.zh: 二十三年九月九日度將士必燕飲，擁勁騎直入南川。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the ninth month of the twenty-third year, reckoning that the officers and troops would surely feast and drink, he led picked cavalry straight into Nanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the Double Ninth Festival of the twenty-third year, calculating that Ming troops would be feasting, he led picked cavalry in a raid on Nanchuan.

sentences.zh: 屬番偵告，雲設兵要害，令番人繞出朶爾硤口外，潛扼其背，而己提精卒二千與戰。

translations.literal: Dependent tribes reported by spies; Yun set troops at strategic points, ordered tribesmen to circle outside Duo'er Gap and secretly seize their rear, while he himself led two thousand picked soldiers into battle.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal allies brought word by scout; Da Yun deployed troops at key passes, sent tribesmen around outside Duo'er Gap to cut off the enemy's retreat, and personally led two thousand elite troops into battle.

sentences.zh: 方合，伏忽起，寇首尾不相顧，番人夾擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Just as the forces met, ambushers suddenly rose; the raiders could not attend to front and rear; tribesmen struck from both sides and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: As the two forces clashed, hidden troops sprang up; the raiders, caught between front and rear, were struck from both sides by the tribesmen and routed.

sentences.zh: 雲手馘其帥一人，斬首六百八十餘級。

translations.literal: Yun with his own hand decapitated one of their chiefs and took more than six hundred eighty heads.
translations.idiomatic: Da Yun personally slew one enemy chieftain and took more than six hundred eighty heads.

sentences.zh: 其走峽外者，又為番人所殲。

translations.literal: Those who fled outside the pass were again annihilated by tribesmen.
translations.idiomatic: Those who escaped the pass were hunted down and killed by the tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 獲駝馬戎器無算。

translations.literal: Camels, horses, and weapons captured were beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: The victors seized camels, horses, and weapons beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 為西陲戰功第一。

translations.literal: It was the foremost military achievement on the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: It ranked as the greatest victory on the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 所馘把都爾哈，即前殺李魁者，其地即魁陣亡處，時又皆九月也。

translations.literal: The one decapitated, Baduerha, was precisely the one who earlier killed Li Kui; the place was precisely where Kui fell in battle, and again it was in the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: The man Da Yun slew, Baduerha, was the very one who had killed Li Kui; the battle was fought where Kui had fallen, and again in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 先是，副將李聯芳為寇所殺，總兵尤繼先生獲其讐。

translations.literal: Earlier, deputy commander Li Lianfang had been killed by raiders, and commander-in-chief You Jixian had earlier taken vengeance on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Previously deputy commander Li Lianfang had been killed by raiders; commander-in-chief You Jixian had already avenged him.

sentences.zh: 邊人以此二事為快。

translations.literal: Frontier people took pleasure in these two affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Along the border these two victories were widely celebrated.

sentences.zh: 雲既勝，度寇必復至，厚集以待。

translations.literal: After Yun had won, he reckoned the raiders would surely return and gathered forces in depth to await them.
translations.idiomatic: After his victory Da Yun expected the raiders to return and massed his forces to meet them.

sentences.zh: 踰月，寇果連真相、火落赤諸部，先圍番剌卜爾寨以誘官軍。

translations.literal: After a month the raiders indeed joined the Zhenxiang, Huoluo Chi, and other divisions, first besieging the Fan Labo'er stockade to lure government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the raiders, joined by the Zhenxiang, Huoluo Chi, and other tribes, besieged the Fan Labo'er stockade to draw out the Ming army.

sentences.zh: 番不能支，合於寇，寇遂逼西川。

translations.literal: The tribes could not hold out, merged with the raiders, and the raiders then pressed upon Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes could not hold; they joined the raiders, who then pressed on toward Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 雲督諸軍營康纏溝，寇悉衆圍之，矢石如雨。

translations.literal: Yun supervised the armies encamped at Kangchan Gully; the raiders mustered all their forces to surround them, arrows and stones falling like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Da Yun drew up his troops at Kangchan Gully; the raiders surrounded them in full force, arrows and stones falling like rain.

sentences.zh: 雲左右衝擊，自辰至申，戰數十合。

translations.literal: Yun struck to left and right; from the chen hour to the shen hour they fought several tens of rounds.
translations.idiomatic: Da Yun charged back and forth from morning till afternoon, fighting dozens of engagements.

sentences.zh: 寇死傷無算，乃以長鎗鈎杆專犯西寧軍。

translations.literal: Raider casualties were beyond count; then with long spears and hook poles they concentrated their attack on the Xining army.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders suffered countless casualties but then concentrated long spears and hook poles against the Xining troops.

sentences.zh: 西寧軍堅不可破，寇始遁，追奔數十里而還。

translations.literal: The Xining army stood firm and could not be broken; the raiders then fled; they pursued fleeing troops several tens of li and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Xining troops held firm; the raiders at last broke and fled, pursued for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，帝大喜，遣官告郊廟，宣捷。

translations.literal: When the victory report arrived, the emperor was greatly pleased, dispatched officials to report at the suburban altars and temples, and proclaimed the triumph.
translations.idiomatic: When word of victory reached the throne, the emperor was overjoyed, ordered sacrifice reported to the suburban altars, and proclaimed the triumph throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 大學士趙志臯以下悉進官。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries beginning with Zhao Zhigao were all promoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao and his colleagues were all promoted.

sentences.zh: 雲擢都督同知，廕本衞世指揮使。

translations.literal: Yun was promoted to vice regional commander; hereditary succession as guard commander of his original guard was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Da Yun was promoted to vice regional commander and granted hereditary succession as guard commander of his home command.

sentences.zh: 寇歲掠諸番，番不敵則折而入寇。

translations.literal: The raiders yearly plundered the various tribes; when tribes could not resist they turned inward to raid.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders plundered the tribes year after year; tribes that could not resist turned to raiding Ming territory instead.

sentences.zh: 及寇敗遠徙，雲急招番，復業者七千餘戶。

translations.literal: When the raiders were defeated and removed far away, Yun urgently recruited tribes; those who resumed livelihood were more than seven thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders were defeated and driven far away, Da Yun urgently resettled the tribes; more than seven thousand households returned to their lands.

sentences.zh: 永邵卜連犯明沙、上谷，雲並擊走之。

translations.literal: Yong Shaobu in succession violated Mingsha and Shanggu; Yun together defeated and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Shaobu raided Mingsha and Shanggu in succession; Da Yun defeated and drove him off both times.

sentences.zh: 初，南川奏捷，雲已進副總兵，至是命以總兵官鎮守延綏。
