translations.literal: Earlier, when Nanchuan reported victory, Yun had already advanced to deputy commander-in-chief; at this time he was ordered as commander-in-chief to garrison Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Nanchuan Da Yun had been promoted to deputy commander-in-chief; now he was appointed commander-in-chief at Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: Before long he commanded Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to command Gansu.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，永邵卜復犯西寧，參將趙希雲等陣歿，雲坐停俸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year Yong Shaobu again violated Xining; assistant commander Zhao Xiyun and others fell in battle; Yun was punished by suspension of salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year Yong Shaobu raided Xining again; assistant commander Zhao Xiyun and others were killed in battle, and Da Yun's pay was suspended.

sentences.zh: 甘、寧間有松山，賓兔、阿赤兔、宰僧、著力兔等居之，屢為兩鎮患。

translations.literal: Between Gansu and Ningxia there is Songshan, where Bin Tu, A Chi Tu, Zai Seng, Zhuo Li Tu, and others dwelt, repeatedly becoming a scourge to the two garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Between Gansu and Ningxia lay Songshan, home to Bin Tu, A Chi Tu, Zai Seng, Zhuo Li Tu, and others, who repeatedly troubled both garrisons.

sentences.zh: 巡撫田樂決策恢復。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Tian Le resolved on recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Tian Le decided to recover the region.

sentences.zh: 雲偕副將甘州馬應龍、涼州姜河、永昌王鐵塊等分道襲之。

translations.literal: Yun together with deputy commanders Ma Yinglong of Ganzhou, Jiang He of Liangzhou, Wang Tiekuai of Yongchang, and others struck by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Da Yun, with deputy commanders Ma Yinglong of Ganzhou, Jiang He of Liangzhou, Wang Tiekuai of Yongchang, and others, attacked by several routes.

sentences.zh: 寇遠竄，盡拔其巢，攘地五百里，雲以功進右都督，廕世指揮僉事。

translations.literal: The raiders fled far; their nests were entirely uprooted; five hundred li of territory was taken; Yun for merit advanced to right regional commander; hereditary assistant guard commander was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders fled deep into the frontier; their strongholds were destroyed and five hundred li of land reclaimed. Da Yun was promoted to right regional commander and granted hereditary succession as assistant guard commander.

sentences.zh: 無何，青海寇糾衆分犯河西，五道俱有備，獻首功百七十有奇。

translations.literal: Before long Qinghai raiders gathered forces and separately violated Hexi; all five routes had preparations; heads presented in merit tallied more than one hundred seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qinghai raiders gathered in force and raided Hexi by several routes; all five columns were ready and more than one hundred seventy heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 松山既復，為築邊垣，分屯置戍。

translations.literal: Once Songshan was recovered, border walls were built, garrisons distributed, and posts set.
translations.idiomatic: After Songshan was recovered, border walls were built and garrisons established throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 錄功進左都督。

translations.literal: Merits were recorded and he advanced to left regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His merits were recorded and he was promoted to left regional commander.

sentences.zh: 寇戀其故巢，乘官軍撤防時潛兵入犯，雲據險邀擊之。

translations.literal: The raiders clung to their old nests; taking advantage of government troops withdrawing defenses they secretly sent troops to raid; Yun seized advantageous terrain to intercept and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders missed their old strongholds; when Ming troops withdrew they raided again in secret, but Da Yun ambushed them from advantageous ground.

sentences.zh: 寇大敗，斬首百六十。

translations.literal: The raiders suffered a great defeat; one hundred sixty heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders were routed and one hundred sixty heads taken.

sentences.zh: 加雲太子少保。

translations.literal: Yun was added the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Da Yun was granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 寇益糾其黨犯鎮番，雲及諸將葛賴等大破之，斬首三百七十餘級。

translations.literal: The raiders further gathered their followers to violate Zhenfan; Yun together with generals Gelai and others inflicted a great defeat; more than three hundred seventy heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders rallied their allies and struck at Zhenfan; Da Yun and general Gelai routed them, taking more than three hundred seventy heads.

sentences.zh: 帝為告廟，行賞，進雲世廕二秩。

translations.literal: The emperor reported at the temples on his behalf, distributed rewards, and advanced Yun's hereditary privilege two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered temple sacrifices, distributed rewards, and advanced Da Yun's hereditary privilege by two ranks.

sentences.zh: 寇復入犯，雲破走之。

translations.literal: The raiders again entered to raid; Yun defeated and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders invaded again, Da Yun defeated and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 是時，寇失松山，走據賀蘭山。

translations.literal: At this time the raiders lost Songshan and fled to occupy Helan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: By then the raiders had lost Songshan and withdrawn to Helan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 後連青海諸部寇鈔不已，銀定、歹成尤桀驁。

translations.literal: Later, joining Qinghai tribes they raided and plundered without cease; Yinding and Daicheng were especially fierce and arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: They then joined with other Qinghai tribes in ceaseless raids; Yinding and Daicheng were the most aggressive.

sentences.zh: 三十三年連營犯鎮番。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year they joined camps to violate Zhenfan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year they encamped together and raided Zhenfan.

sentences.zh: 雲遣副將柴國柱擊之，寇大敗去。

translations.literal: Yun dispatched deputy commander Chai Guozhu to strike them; the raiders suffered a great defeat and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Da Yun sent deputy commander Chai Guozhu against them; the raiders were routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，青海寇復大入，將士分道遮擊，生禽其長沙賴，餘敗奔。

translations.literal: Before long Qinghai raiders again entered in strength; officers and troops intercepted by separate routes; their chief Shalai was captured alive; the rest were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qinghai raiders invaded again in force; Ming troops intercepted them on several routes, captured their chieftain Shalai alive, and routed the rest.

sentences.zh: 三十五年敘功，雲增勳廕。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year merits were reviewed; Yun's merit fief and hereditary privilege were increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year his achievements were rewarded and his merit fief increased.

sentences.zh: 是年，松山、青海二寇復連兵犯涼州，雲逆戰紅崖，大獲，斬首百三十有奇。

translations.literal: That year the two raiders of Songshan and Qinghai again joined forces to violate Liangzhou; Yun countered them at Hongya, won greatly, and took more than one hundred thirty heads.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Songshan and Qinghai raiders joined forces and struck Liangzhou; Da Yun met them at Hongya, won a great victory, and took more than one hundred thirty heads.

sentences.zh: 雲為將，先登陷陣，所至未嘗挫衂，名震西陲，為一時邊將之冠。

translations.literal: Yun as a general was first to ascend and break formations; wherever he went he never suffered setback; his fame shook the western frontier; he was the crown of frontier generals of the age.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander Da Yun always led the charge; he never knew defeat wherever he was posted. His fame resounded across the western frontier, and he stood foremost among the border generals of his age.

sentences.zh: 以秋防卒於軍。

translations.literal: He died in camp during autumn defense.
translations.idiomatic: He died on campaign during autumn border duty.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子奇勛，萬曆末為昌平總兵官。

translations.literal: His son Qixun was at the end of Wanli commander-in-chief of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qixun served at the end of the Wanli reign as commander-in-chief of Changping.

sentences.zh: 尤繼先

translations.literal: You Jixian
translations.idiomatic: You Jixian

sentences.zh: 尤繼先，榆林衞人。

translations.literal: You Jixian was a native of Yulin Guard.
translations.idiomatic: You Jixian was a native of Yulin Guard.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，積功為大同副總兵。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign, through accumulated merit he became deputy commander-in-chief of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he rose through merit to deputy commander-in-chief of Datong.

sentences.zh: 十八年，火落赤、真相犯洮、河，副總兵李聯芳等戰死。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Huoluo Chi and Zhenxiang violated Tao and He; deputy commander Li Lianfang and others died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Huoluo Chi and Zhenxiang raided the Tao and He region; deputy commander Li Lianfang and others were killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 詔進署都督僉事，充總兵官，代劉承嗣鎮守固原。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to acting assistant regional commander, appointed him commander-in-chief, and he replaced Liu Chengsi in garrisoning Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting assistant regional commander and appointed commander-in-chief at Guyuan in place of Liu Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 寇據莽剌、捏工二川，日蠶食番族，且擾西寧。

translations.literal: The raiders occupied Mangla and Nie Gong two valleys, daily nibbling away at tribal peoples, and also harassed Xining.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders held the Mangla and Nie Gong valleys, steadily encroaching on tribal lands and harassing Xining.

sentences.zh: 聞官軍大集，卜失兔又敗於水泉，乃乘冰堅渡黃河北走，留其黨可卜列、宗塔兒等五百餘人牧莽剌川南山。

translations.literal: Hearing that government troops were massing, and that Bu Shitu had again been defeated at Shuiquan, they crossed the Yellow River north on solid ice and fled, leaving their followers Kebulie, Zong Ta'er, and more than five hundred others to pasture at the southern mountains of Mangla Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Ming forces were massing and that Bu Shitu had been defeated again at Shuiquan, they crossed the frozen Yellow River and fled north, leaving more than five hundred followers including Kebulie and Zong Ta'er to pasture in the southern hills of Mangla Valley.

sentences.zh: 南山即石門大山口，走烏思藏門戶也。

translations.literal: The southern mountains were precisely the Shimen Great Mountain Pass, the gateway to U-Tsang.
translations.idiomatic: Those southern hills were the Shimen Great Pass, the gateway to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 屬番來告，繼先乃令番以八百人前導，與故總兵承嗣，遊擊原進學、吳顯等疾馳七百里，直抵南山。

translations.literal: Dependent tribes came to report; Jixian then ordered tribesmen with eight hundred men to lead the way, and together with the former commander-in-chief Chengsi, mobile corps commander Yuan Jinxue, Wu Xian, and others galloped seven hundred li, reaching the southern mountains straight on.
translations.idiomatic: When tribal allies brought word, Jixian sent eight hundred tribesmen as guides and, with former commander-in-chief Chengsi and mobile corps commanders Yuan Jinxue and Wu Xian, rode seven hundred li straight to the southern hills.

sentences.zh: 奮擊，大破之，斬首百五十有奇，生獲十二人。

translations.literal: They struck fiercely, inflicted a great defeat, and took more than one hundred fifty heads; twelve were captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked with fury, routed the enemy, took more than one hundred fifty heads, and captured twelve alive.

sentences.zh: 而拜巴爾的者，可卜列從子，前殺聯芳，至是被禽。

translations.literal: Baiba'erde was Kebulie's nephew; he had earlier killed Lianfang, and now was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Baiba'erde, Kebulie's nephew, who had killed Lianfang, was among those captured.

sentences.zh: 師旋，寇尾至撒川。

translations.literal: As the army withdrew, raiders followed to the rear as far as Sachuan.
translations.idiomatic: As the army withdrew, raiders pursued as far as Sachuan.

sentences.zh: 見有備，乃夜走。

translations.literal: Seeing preparations in place, they fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the Ming forces ready, they fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 他寇犯鎮羌、西寧、石羊亦俱敗。

translations.literal: Other raiders who violated Zhenqiang, Xining, and Shiyang were likewise defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Other raiders who struck at Zhenqiang, Xining, and Shiyang were defeated as well.

sentences.zh: 火落赤遂徙帳西海。

translations.literal: Huoluo Chi then moved his camp to the Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Huoluo Chi then moved his encampment to Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進秩為真，增世廕一秩。

translations.literal: Merits were recorded; his rank became substantive, and hereditary privilege was increased one rank.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were recorded; his acting rank was made permanent and his hereditary privilege increased by one rank.

sentences.zh: 尋以病歸。

translations.literal: Soon he returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 起僉中軍府事。

translations.literal: He was raised to serve in the Central Military Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve in the Central Military Bureau.

sentences.zh: 二十一年冬為遼東總兵官。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-first year he became commander-in-chief of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twenty-first year he was appointed commander-in-chief of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 炒花二千騎入韓家路，繼先督諸軍奮擊，寇乃去。

translations.literal: Chaohua with two thousand horsemen entered Hanjia Road; Jixian supervised the armies in fierce attack, and the raiders then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Chaohua led two thousand horsemen into Hanjia Road; Jixian led the troops in a fierce counterattack and the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 再引疾歸。

translations.literal: Again he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He again pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 二十四年起鎮薊州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was raised to command Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was recalled to command Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 自戚繼光鎮守十年，諸部雖叛服不常，然邊警頗稀。

translations.literal: Since Qi Jiguang had garrisoned for ten years, the various tribes though rebellious and submissive by turns, yet frontier alarms were rather few.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qi Jiguang had held the garrison for ten years, the tribes remained restive but border alarms were infrequent.

sentences.zh: 寇嘗一入青山口，輒敗去。

translations.literal: When raiders once entered Qingshan Pass they were immediately defeated and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders once entered Qingshan Pass they were beaten back at once.

sentences.zh: 最後，長昂導班、白二部長入犯，道石門，闞山海關，京東民盡逃入通州。

translations.literal: Finally, Chang Ang guided the Ban and Bai chieftains to invade; they passed through Shimen, blocked Shanhaiguan, and people east of the capital all fled into Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At last Chang Ang led the Ban and Bai chieftains in an invasion; they passed Shimen, threatened Shanhaiguan, and people throughout the eastern capital fled into Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 繼先出關，寇已縱掠寧前去。

translations.literal: Jixian went out of the pass; the raiders had already freely plundered and gone toward Ningqian.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian marched out of the pass, but the raiders had already finished plundering and withdrawn toward Ningqian.

sentences.zh: 總督蹇達怒繼先不追擊，而繼先方收召降丁八百人，欲倚為用。

translations.literal: Governor-general Jian Da was angry that Jixian did not pursue and attack, while Jixian was just gathering eight hundred surrendered tribesmen, intending to rely on them for use.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Jian Da was furious that Jixian had not pursued, while Jixian was busy recruiting eight hundred surrendered tribesmen he hoped to employ.

sentences.zh: 達乃疏言番情難馭，恐遺後憂，請調繼先別鎮，俾降丁隨往。

translations.literal: Da then memorialized saying tribal sentiments were hard to control, fearing leaving later worries, and requested transferring Jixian to another garrison, letting surrendered tribesmen follow him there.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Da memorialized that tribal auxiliaries were unreliable and might cause future trouble, and asked that Jixian be transferred elsewhere with the surrendered tribesmen in tow.

sentences.zh: 部議以延綏杜松與易任，巡撫劉四科爭之。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated to exchange him with Du Song of Yan-sui; grand coordinator Liu Sike contested it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry proposed swapping him with Du Song of Yan-sui, but Grand Coordinator Liu Sike objected.

sentences.zh: 達復疏言：「守邊在自強，繼先獨言惟藉降丁。

translations.literal: Da again memorialized saying: "Defending the border lies in strengthening oneself; Jixian alone says one must rely only on surrendered tribesmen.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Da memorialized again: "Border defense depends on self-reliance, yet Jixian insists that one can rely only on surrendered tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 去歲出關，何竟不得降丁力？

translations.literal: Last year going out of the pass, why did he ultimately not obtain the strength of surrendered tribesmen?
translations.idiomatic: When he marched out last year, where was the strength of those surrendered tribesmen?

sentences.zh: 羽書狎至，邊隘虛實久為所窺。

translations.literal: Urgent dispatches arrive one after another; the emptiness and fullness of border passes have long been spied out by them.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent dispatches arrive incessantly; the enemy has long known every weakness of our border defenses.

sentences.zh: 呼吸變生，安所措手！」

translations.literal: Changes arise in a breath — where can one set hand to act!"
translations.idiomatic: Disaster can strike in an instant — how is one to respond!

sentences.zh: 兵科宋一韓等力主達議，且劾繼先他事。

translations.literal: The military affairs censor Song Yihan and others strongly upheld Da's proposal and also impeached Jixian on other matters.
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs Censor Song Yihan and others strongly supported Jian Da's proposal and also impeached Jixian on other grounds.

sentences.zh: 繼先遂罷，卒於家。

translations.literal: Jixian was then dismissed and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian was dismissed and died at home.

sentences.zh: 繼先眇一目，習兵敢戰，時稱「獨目將軍」。

translations.literal: Jixian was blind in one eye, versed in military affairs and bold in battle; at the time he was called the "One-Eyed General."
translations.idiomatic: Blind in one eye, skilled in war and fearless in battle, he was known as the "One-Eyed General."

sentences.zh: 官秉忠

translations.literal: Guan Bingzhong
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bingzhong

sentences.zh: 官秉忠，榆林衞人。

translations.literal: Guan Bingzhong was a native of Yulin Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bingzhong was a native of Yulin Guard.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中起世廕，歷官固原參將，擢寧夏、甘肅副總兵。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he rose through hereditary privilege, served as assistant commander at Guyuan, and was promoted to deputy commander-in-chief of Ningxia and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he entered service through hereditary privilege, rose to assistant commander at Guyuan, and was promoted to deputy commander-in-chief of Ningxia and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 嘗與主將達雲大破寇於紅崖，銀定、歹成屢被挫去。

translations.literal: He once together with commander-in-chief Da Yun inflicted a great defeat on raiders at Hongya; Yinding and Daicheng were repeatedly beaten and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: He had joined commander-in-chief Da Yun in a great victory at Hongya, repeatedly routing Yinding and Daicheng.

sentences.zh: 移守薊鎮東協，積功加署都督同知。

translations.literal: He was transferred to guard the eastern wing of Jizhen and through accumulated merit was added the acting rank of vice regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the eastern wing of Jizhen, he rose through merit to acting vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 四十年五月，擢總兵官，代張承廕鎮延綏。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fortieth year he was promoted to commander-in-chief, replacing Zhang Chengyin in commanding Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fortieth year he was promoted to commander-in-chief at Yan-sui, replacing Zhang Chengyin.

sentences.zh: 套寇犯保寧，秉忠督參將杜文煥等敗之白土澗。

translations.literal: Ordos raiders violated Baoning; Bingzhong supervised assistant commander Du Wenhuan and others in defeating them at Baitu Stream.
translations.idiomatic: When Ordos raiders struck Baoning, Bingzhong led assistant commander Du Wenhuan and others to defeat them at Baitu Stream.

sentences.zh: 一日再捷，俘斬二百五十，馘其長十二人。

translations.literal: Two victories in one day; two hundred fifty captured and slain; twelve of their chiefs decapitated.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day he won two victories, capturing or slaying two hundred fifty and decapitating twelve enemy chiefs.

sentences.zh: 無何，旗牌撒勒犯長樂，秉忠將輕騎追襲之，大獲。

translations.literal: Before long the banner chief Sale violated Changlo; Bingzhong led picked cavalry in pursuit and struck them, winning greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the banner chief Sale raided Changlo; Bingzhong led picked cavalry in pursuit and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 猛克什力犯保寧，秉忠又破之。

translations.literal: Mengke Shili violated Baoning; Bingzhong again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengke Shili raided Baoning, Bingzhong defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 已而猛克挾賞不獲，再寇保寧及懷遠，秉忠隨所向以勁騎遮擊，先後斬首二百二十有奇。

translations.literal: Before long Mengke, having failed to obtain rewards, again raided Baoning and Huaiyuan; Bingzhong wherever they went intercepted with picked cavalry, successively taking more than two hundred twenty heads.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengke, denied the rewards he demanded, raided Baoning and Huaiyuan again, Bingzhong intercepted his picked cavalry wherever they struck, taking more than two hundred twenty heads in all.

sentences.zh: 猛克及旗牌復以千餘騎犯波羅，遙見保寧軍，遂遁出塞。

translations.literal: Mengke and the banner chiefs again with more than a thousand horsemen violated Boluo; seeing Baoning troops from afar, they then fled out of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Mengke and the banner chiefs raided Boluo with more than a thousand horsemen but fled back across the border at the sight of Baoning troops.

sentences.zh: 吉能者，卜失兔子，為套中之主，士馬雄諸部。

translations.literal: Jineng was Bu Shitu's son, master of the Ordos, with soldiers and horses surpassing all divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Jineng, son of Bu Shitu, was lord of the Ordos and commanded the strongest force among the tribes.

sentences.zh: 見卜失兔襲順義王，補其五年市賞，遂挾求封王，且還八年市賞。

translations.literal: Seeing Bu Shitu attack the Prince of Shunyi and make up his five years of market rewards, he then seized the occasion to demand enfeoffment as prince and also the return of eight years of market rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Bu Shitu attacked the Prince of Shunyi and received five years of back pay in border-market rewards, Jineng demanded enfeoffment as a prince and eight years of market rewards as well.

sentences.zh: 邊臣不許，則大怨。

translations.literal: Frontier officials did not permit it, and he then greatly resented.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials refused, and he flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 會他部鐵雷以痘瘡死，妄言邊吏毒殺之。

translations.literal: It happened that another division's Tie Lei died of smallpox; they falsely claimed frontier officials had poisoned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: About then Tie Lei of another tribe died of smallpox; the tribes falsely claimed border officials had poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 而沙計盜邊，又被衂去。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Shaji raided the border and was again driven off in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Shaji raided the border and was humiliatingly driven off.

sentences.zh: 吉能遂合套中諸部，大舉入寇。

translations.literal: Jineng then joined all divisions within the Ordos and entered to raid on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Jineng then rallied all the Ordos tribes in a major invasion.

sentences.zh: 東道高家、大柏油、神木、柏林，中道波羅，西道磚井、寧塞諸城堡盡被蹂躪。

translations.literal: The eastern route's Gaojia, Dabaiyou, Shenmu, and Bailing, the central route's Boluo, and the western route's Zhuanjing, Ningsai, and other forts and castles were all trampled.
translations.idiomatic: Forts along the eastern route — Gaojia, Dabaiyou, Shenmu, Bailing — the central route at Boluo, and the western route at Zhuanjing, Ningsai, and elsewhere were all ravaged.

sentences.zh: 副將孫洪謨禦之大柏油，中伏被圍。

translations.literal: Deputy commander Sun Hongmo defended at Dabaiyou and was ambushed and surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Sun Hongmo defended Dabaiyou but was ambushed and surrounded.

sentences.zh: 遊擊萬化孚等不救，士卒死傷過半，洪謨遂降。

translations.literal: Mobile corps commander Wan Huafu and others did not rescue; more than half the soldiers were killed and wounded; Hongmo then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile corps commander Wan Huafu and others failed to relieve him; more than half his men were killed or wounded, and Hongmo surrendered.

sentences.zh: 秉忠聞寇入，急遣遊擊張榜潛劫其營，又敗，死四百餘人。

translations.literal: Bingzhong, hearing raiders had entered, urgently dispatched mobile corps commander Zhang Bang to secretly raid their camp; again defeated, more than four hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingzhong learned of the invasion, he sent mobile corps commander Zhang Bang to raid the enemy camp by stealth; the raid failed and more than four hundred men were lost.

sentences.zh: 會故帥杜松、寧夏帥杜文煥援軍至，竝破敵，而秉忠所部亦有斬獲，寇始退。

translations.literal: Then former commander Du Song and Ningxia commander Du Wenhuan's relief armies arrived; together they broke the enemy, and Bingzhong's own division also had captures and kills; the raiders then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Former commander Du Song and Ningxia commander Du Wenhuan arrived with reinforcements; together they broke the enemy. Bingzhong's troops also took heads, and the raiders at last withdrew.

sentences.zh: 然猶駐塞下，時鈔掠。

translations.literal: Yet they still encamped below the frontier, plundering from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: They remained camped below the border, raiding whenever they could.

sentences.zh: 秉忠亦屢出襲擊，多獲首功，竟以前負被劾去官。

translations.literal: Bingzhong also repeatedly went out to raid and strike, often gaining heads in merit, yet ultimately was impeached and removed from office on account of earlier failures.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhong led repeated counter-raids and took many heads, but was impeached and dismissed for his earlier losses.

sentences.zh: 方候代，沙計謀從雙山、建安入犯，秉忠設伏待之。

translations.literal: While awaiting replacement, Shaji plotted to enter from Shuangshan and Jian'an; Bingzhong set an ambush to await them.
translations.idiomatic: While awaiting his successor, Shaji planned to invade through Shuangshan and Jian'an; Bingzhong laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 遂大敗去，斬其首二百有奇。

translations.literal: They then suffered a great defeat and departed; more than two hundred heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders were routed and more than two hundred heads taken.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，與劉綎、柴國柱等同被召，令僉書前府，尋赴援遼東。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he was summoned together with Liu Ting, Chai Guozhu, and others, ordered to serve as assistant in the Front Bureau, and soon went to aid Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year he was summoned with Liu Ting, Chai Guozhu, and others to serve in the Front Bureau and soon marched to aid Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 楊鎬之四路出師也，令秉忠防守鎮城。

translations.literal: When Yang Hao dispatched the four-route army, Bingzhong was ordered to defend Zhencheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Hao launched his four-route campaign, Bingzhong was ordered to hold Zhencheng.

sentences.zh: 無何，辭疾歸。

translations.literal: Before long he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died some years later.

sentences.zh: 子撫民，亦為寧夏總兵官。

translations.literal: His son Fumin also became commander-in-chief of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fumin also served as commander-in-chief of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 柴國柱

translations.literal: Chai Guozhu
translations.idiomatic: Chai Guozhu

sentences.zh: 柴國柱，西寧衞人。

translations.literal: Chai Guozhu was a native of Xining Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Guozhu was a native of Xining Guard.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，由世廕歷西寧守備。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign, through hereditary privilege he successively served as garrison commandant of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he entered service through hereditary privilege and rose to garrison commandant of Xining.

sentences.zh: 驍猛善射。

translations.literal: Valiant and fierce, skilled in archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was valiant, fierce, and an expert archer.

sentences.zh: 從參將達雲擊寇南川，勇冠軍。

translations.literal: Following assistant commander Da Yun he struck raiders at Nanchuan; his courage topped the army.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under assistant commander Da Yun at Nanchuan, his courage outshone every man in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Merits were recorded; he advanced to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were recorded and he was promoted to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 寇盜邊，輒為國柱所挫。

translations.literal: When raiders plundered the border they were always beaten back by Guozhu.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever raiders struck the border, Guozhu drove them back.

sentences.zh: 屢進涼州副總兵。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander-in-chief of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to deputy commander-in-chief of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 松山既復，方建堡置堠，寇數來擾，國柱頻擊却之。

translations.literal: Once Songshan was recovered, as forts and beacon towers were being built, raiders came several times to harass; Guozhu frequently struck and repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: After Songshan was recovered and new forts and beacon towers were going up, raiders harassed the works repeatedly; Guozhu beat them back each time.

sentences.zh: 銀定、歹成連兵寇鎮番，國柱馳救，斬首二百有奇，獲馬駝甲仗無算。

translations.literal: Yinding and Daicheng joined forces to raid Zhenfan; Guozhu galloped to the rescue, took more than two hundred heads, and seized horses, camels, armor, and weapons beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinding and Daicheng joined forces against Zhenfan, Guozhu rode to the rescue, took more than two hundred heads, and seized horses, camels, armor, and weapons beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 青海寇大掠鎮羌、黑古城諸堡，守備楊國珍不能禦，國柱急率遊擊王允中等擊走之。

translations.literal: Qinghai raiders greatly plundered the forts of Zhenqiang, Heigucheng, and others; garrison commandant Yang Guozhen could not resist; Guozhu urgently led mobile corps commander Wang Yunzhong and others to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinghai raiders ravaged Zhenqiang, Heigucheng, and other forts and garrison commandant Yang Guozhen could not hold, Guozhu rushed in with mobile corps commander Wang Yunzhong and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 銀定、歹成復犯河西，國柱邀擊，獲首功百二十。

translations.literal: Yinding and Daicheng again violated Hexi; Guozhu intercepted and struck; one hundred twenty heads were taken in merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinding and Daicheng raided Hexi again, Guozhu intercepted them and took one hundred twenty heads.

sentences.zh: 擢署都督僉事，陝西總兵官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting assistant regional commander and commander-in-chief of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting assistant regional commander and commander-in-chief of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 三十六年春，改鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirty-sixth year he was transferred to command Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirty-sixth year he was transferred to command Gansu.

sentences.zh: 銀定、歹成屢不得志，益寇鈔永昌。

translations.literal: Yinding and Daicheng, repeatedly frustrated, all the more raided and plundered Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated again and again, Yinding and Daicheng redoubled their raids on Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 國柱馳與大戰，敗之，追至麻山湖，斬首百六十有奇。

translations.literal: Guozhu galloped to join in great battle, defeated them, pursued to Mayingshan Lake, and took more than one hundred sixty heads.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu rode to meet them in battle, routed them, pursued them to Mayingshan Lake, and took more than one hundred sixty heads.

sentences.zh: 其部落復入寇，守備鄭崇雅等戰歿，國柱坐奪俸一年。

translations.literal: Their tribes again entered to raid; garrison commandant Zheng Chongya and others died in battle; Guozhu was punished by deduction of salary for one year.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes raided again and garrison commandant Zheng Chongya and others were killed, Guozhu's pay was docked for a year.

sentences.zh: 河套、松山諸部長合兵入寇，國柱檄諸將分道擊，復斬首百六十。

translations.literal: Chieftains of the Ordos, Songshan, and other divisions joined forces to raid; Guozhu dispatched generals to strike by separate routes and again took one hundred sixty heads.
translations.idiomatic: When Ordos and Songshan chieftains joined in a raid, Guozhu sent his generals against them on several routes and took another one hundred sixty heads.

sentences.zh: 屢加右都督，世廕指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly added right regional commander; hereditary assistant guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted, reaching right regional commander with hereditary succession as assistant guard commander.

sentences.zh: 久之，罷官。

translations.literal: After long time he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 四十六年夏，召僉書都督府事。

translations.literal: In the summer of the forty-sixth year he was summoned to serve as assistant in the Regional Commander's Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the forty-sixth year he was summoned to serve in the Regional Commander's Bureau.

sentences.zh: 無何，代杜松鎮山海關。

translations.literal: Before long he replaced Du Song in commanding Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he replaced Du Song as commander of Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 松敗歿，虎墩兔乘機犯邊，國柱等力遏之。

translations.literal: When Du Song was defeated and died, Huduntu seized the occasion to violate the border; Guozhu and others forcefully checked them.
translations.idiomatic: After Du Song's defeat and death, Huduntu seized the moment to raid the border; Guozhu and his colleagues held the line.

sentences.zh: 尋移鎮瀋陽。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to command Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to command Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 謝病歸。

translations.literal: He cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追錄邊功，加左都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, frontier merits were posthumously recorded; he was added left regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi his frontier achievements were recorded and he was promoted to left regional commander.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜恤如制。

translations.literal: He died; condolences and grants were bestowed according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was granted posthumous honors according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 李懷信

translations.literal: Li Huaixin
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaixin

sentences.zh: 李懷信，大同人。

translations.literal: Li Huaixin was a native of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaixin was a native of Datong.

sentences.zh: 由世廕歷都指揮僉事，掌山西都司。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he successively served as assistant regional commander and directed the Shanxi Regional Commander's Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he rose to assistant regional commander and director of the Shanxi military command.

sentences.zh: 廉勤，數被推薦。

translations.literal: Honest and diligent, he was repeatedly recommended.
translations.idiomatic: Honest and diligent, he was repeatedly recommended for promotion.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，遷延綏中路參將，進定邊副總兵。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he was transferred to assistant commander of the central route at Yan-sui and advanced to deputy commander-in-chief of Dingbian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he was posted as assistant commander on Yan-sui's central route and promoted to deputy commander-in-chief of Dingbian.

sentences.zh: 卜失兔、火落赤、鐵雷、擺言太等歲擾邊。

translations.literal: Bu Shitu, Huoluo Chi, Tie Lei, Baiyan Tai, and others yearly harassed the border.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Shitu, Huoluo Chi, Tie Lei, Baiyan Tai, and others raided the border year after year.

sentences.zh: 定邊居延綏西，被患尤棘。

translations.literal: Dingbian lay west of Yan-sui and suffered the border affliction especially keenly.
translations.idiomatic: Dingbian, west of Yan-sui, bore the brunt of the border troubles.

sentences.zh: 懷信勇敢有謀，寇入輒敗。

translations.literal: Huaixin was brave and possessed stratagem; whenever raiders entered they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and resourceful, Huaixin defeated every raider who crossed the border.

sentences.zh: 其先後鎮帥杜松、王威、張承廕、官秉忠又皆一時選，故邊患雖劇，而士氣不衰。

translations.literal: The commanders who successively commanded there — Du Song, Wang Wei, Zhang Chengyin, and Guan Bingzhong — were all chosen men of the age, so though border troubles were severe, troop morale did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: His successive superiors — Du Song, Wang Wei, Zhang Chengyin, and Guan Bingzhong — were all elite commanders of the day, so despite severe border troubles morale never flagged.

sentences.zh: 四十三年擢甘肅總兵官，延人為立生祠。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was promoted to commander-in-chief of Gansu; the people extended an invitation to erect a living shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was promoted to commander-in-chief of Gansu; local people petitioned to build a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 松山寇入掠蘆溝墩諸處，懷信邀擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Songshan raiders entered to plunder Lucun Dun and other places; Huaixin intercepted and struck; they suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Songshan raiders plundered Lucun Dun and neighboring posts, Huaixin intercepted them and routed them.

sentences.zh: 斬首三百有奇，獲駝馬甲仗無算。

translations.literal: More than three hundred heads were taken; camels, horses, armor, and weapons captured were beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: He took more than three hundred heads and seized camels, horses, armor, and weapons beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 已，復分三道犯鎮番諸堡，懷信亦分遏之。

translations.literal: Before long they again divided into three routes to violate the forts of Zhenfan; Huaixin also divided forces to check them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the raiders split into three columns against the Zhenfan forts; Huaixin divided his forces to block each one.

sentences.zh: 寇引還，將士尾其後，獲首功百九十有奇。

translations.literal: The raiders withdrew; officers and troops followed their rear and took more than one hundred ninety heads in merit.
translations.idiomatic: As the raiders withdrew, Ming troops pursued and took more than one hundred ninety heads.

sentences.zh: 自後寇入多失利去，威名著河西。

translations.literal: Afterward when raiders entered they mostly departed having lost; his prestige was famed in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter raiders who entered Hexi usually withdrew in defeat; his reputation resounded throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 先是，陝西止設四鎮，自西寧多警，增設臨洮總兵官，遂為五鎮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shaanxi had only four garrisons; because Xining had many alarms, a commander-in-chief of Lintao was added, making five garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi had originally maintained four garrisons; as Xining grew restless a fifth was added at Lintao.

sentences.zh: 然惟甘、延最當敵衝，故擇帥常慎。

translations.literal: Yet only Gansu and Yan-sui were most directly in the path of the enemy; hence choosing commanders was always done with care.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gansu and Yan-sui lay directly in the enemy's path, and commanders for those posts were chosen with especial care.

sentences.zh: 而甘肅北有松山，南臨青海，諸部落環居其外，尤難禦。

translations.literal: Yet Gansu had Songshan to the north and faced Qinghai to the south, with tribal encampments ringed around outside; it was especially hard to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu was especially difficult to hold: Songshan to the north, Qinghai to the south, and tribal camps encircling it on every side.

sentences.zh: 懷信在鎮，邊人恃以無恐。

translations.literal: While Huaixin held the garrison, border people relied on him without fear.
translations.idiomatic: While Huaixin commanded the garrison, the border people lived without fear.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，遼東急，詔充援勦總兵官，馳赴遼東。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year Liaodong was urgent; an edict appointed him relief-and-suppression commander-in-chief, galloping to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year, with Liaodong in crisis, he was appointed relief commander-in-chief and rushed to the northeast.

sentences.zh: 時熊廷弼為經略，令懷信偕柴國柱、賀世賢以四萬人守瀋陽。

translations.literal: At the time Xiong Tingbi was grand coordinator; he ordered Huaixin together with Chai Guozhu and He Shixian to hold Shenyang with forty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Xiong Tingbi ordered Huaixin, Chai Guozhu, and He Shixian to hold Shenyang with forty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 煖兔、炒花謀入犯，廷弼急移懷信戍首山，寇不敢入。

translations.literal: Nuannu and Chaohua plotted to enter and raid; Tingbi urgently moved Huaixin to garrison Shoushan; the raiders did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Nuannu and Chaohua plotted an invasion, Tingbi rushed Huaixin to Shoushan and the raiders dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 俄泛懿有警，檄懷信禦却之。

translations.literal: Soon Fan Yi had an alarm; an order dispatched Huaixin to repulse them.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yi came under threat, Huaixin was ordered to repulse the enemy.

sentences.zh: 遼事益急，諸老將多引避。

translations.literal: Liao affairs grew ever more urgent; many old generals mostly cited illness to avoid service.
translations.idiomatic: As the Liaodong crisis deepened, many veteran generals pleaded illness to stay away.

sentences.zh: 廷弼復負氣凌諸將，懷信不能堪，亦堅臥引疾去。

translations.literal: Tingbi again bore an arrogant temperament and looked down on the generals; Huaixin could not endure it and also lay firm in bed citing illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tingbi's arrogance toward his subordinates became unbearable; Huaixin too pleaded illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年起鎮大同。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was raised to command Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he was recalled to command Datong.

sentences.zh: 明年罷。

translations.literal: The following year he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 已，追錄邊功，進左都督。

translations.literal: Before long, frontier merits were posthumously recorded; he advanced to left regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward his frontier achievements were recorded posthumously and he was promoted to left regional commander.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒於家。

translations.literal: After a long while he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home some years later.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：張臣諸人，勇略自奮，著效邊陲，均一時良將選也。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Zhang Chen and the others, through their own valor and strategy, achieved distinction on the frontier and all ranked among the chosen fine generals of their age.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Zhang Chen and his fellows, driving themselves by courage and strategy, won distinction along the frontier and all belonged among the finest commanders of their day.

sentences.zh: 董一元白沙堝、墨山之捷，奇偉不下王越。

translations.literal: Dong Yiyuan's victories at Baisha'ao and Mo Mountain were as marvelous and grand as those of Wang Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yiyuan's victories at Baisha'ao and Mo Mountain were as brilliant as any won by Wang Yue.

sentences.zh: 至承廕與松，以將門子捐軀報國，視世所稱「東李西麻」者，相去何等也。

translations.literal: As for Chengyin and Song, who as sons of generals gave their lives to repay the state, how vast is the distance between them and those whom the age calls "Li of the east and Ma of the west"!
translations.idiomatic: As for Chengyin and Song, who as sons of commanders gave their lives for the state, how far they stand from the fame of the age's "Li in the east and Ma in the west"!
